articles.title: Why Africa needs its own AI off switch
articles.summary:
Imagine that it is 6 a.m. in the wholesale markets of Nairobi. Merchants are delivering vegetables from up-country farms to the retailers who sell to the city’s households. Everyone is using M-Pesa, Safaricom’s mobile money platform, when suddenly, the system crashes, bringing the market to a standstill. Imagine that across the continent in Accra, MTN’s MoMo has also crashed, and business in Makola Market has all but stopped.
With the growing number of cyberattacks caused by artificial intelligence, these are highly plausible scenarios. In both these cases, Safaricom, MTN, and the Kenyan and Ghanaian governments need an off switch, or the technical ability and know-how to stop a rogue AI agent from executing its code on their payment systems.
Currently, the conversation on AI agents revolves around China versus the U.S., open versus closed models, and who will dominate the AI race. But in Africa’s capitals, the distinction that will ultimately matter is not whose product was used to build a system, or who dominates whom, but rather whether AI can serve its purpose and be controlled locally. So how can Africa build with agency, and with control over the code and makeup of its own systems, even though they are built on foreign technology?
African countries are already building AI for digital transformation, as outlined in the African Union’s continental AI strategy and country-specific AI strategies. Policymakers are building AI infrastructure but rarely discuss how AI delivers…

articles.title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
articles.summary:
Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
Welcome to the 26th edition of Cloudflare's DDoS Threat Report. This edition covers the third quarter of 2026 — July, August, and September — and returns the series to its quarterly cadence following the combined H1 2026 volume. The analysis is produced by Cloudforce One, Cloudflare's Threat Intelligence organization, providing a comprehensive analysis of the evolving threat landscape of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks based on data from the Cloudflare network.
Key insights
- Short-burst, low-bandwidth attacks lasting under 10 minutes and 1 Gbps surged by 208%. Conversely, hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps plummeted by nearly 69% from Q2, possibly a reflection of law enforcement actions against four major Internet of Things (IoT) botnets earlier in the year. However, variants continue to emerge, proving that IoT botnets remain a durable, high-volume threat to network infrastructure.
- Threat actors dramatically shifted their reflection and amplification tactics, abruptly abandoning CLDAP floods, which collapsed by 99.5% quarter-over-quarter. Instead, attackers pivoted heavily toward other connectionless protocols, driving a 215% surge in DNS amplification and a 122% increase in general UDP floods.

articles.title: 3 Ways AI Agents Already Operate in Your Browser
articles.summary:
Which AI agents can act inside your employees' browsers today? If an agent started browsing this morning, would you know it wasn't the employee? Most security teams can't answer those questions yet. That's not a failure of effort. It's a sign of how quickly AI moved from answering questions to taking action.
AI agents now operate browsers inside authenticated applications, and they get there in different ways: debugging interfaces, extensions, agentic browsers, and emerging standards like WebMCP. Each changes what an agent can access, how its actions are attributed, and whether existing controls can see them.
1. Remote Debugging: Applications Controlling the Browser
One way AI agents operate browsers isn't new at all. It's the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
CDP was built to help developers inspect, debug, and automate Chromium-based browsers. It provides programmatic access to navigation, page content, network activity, and user interactions. Tools like Playwright and Puppeteer have used it for years. AI agents use the same approach to navigate websites, extract information, fill forms, and interact with web applications.
The key distinction: automation doesn't have to originate inside the browser. An external application can connect to a browser with debugging enabled and control its tabs. If that browser has authenticated sessions, the automation can use that access.

The app connects to Instagram to build a virtual closet from photos you’ve posted, or lets you add items manually by snapping a photo, recording a quick video, or uploading images from your camera roll.
Style Sketch then suggests outfit combinations built from your wardrobe matched to your style. Users can then try on the outfits on a “realistic model matched to your body shape and skin tone,” the app description reads.
The app, which was first spotted by social media consultant Matt Navarra, is available in Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand on iOS and Android.
Meta did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment. It’s unknown whether Meta plans to launch Style Sketch more widely.
Several apps already use AI to help users digitize their wardrobes and visualize new outfits, including startups like Alta. Even Google Photos offers tools that let users turn photos of their clothes into digital closets where they can create new outfit ideas.
To compete with what’s already on the market, Meta will likely rely less on the novelty of the idea and more on the app’s integration with Instagram, where users already have a visual record of their personal style.

articles.summary:
Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: Google Touts Powerful Cybersecurity Capabilities in Gemini 4 Carbon Model
articles.summary:
Google on Wednesday announced Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier AI model that, according to the company, beats rival models on benchmarks for detecting, exploiting and patching vulnerabilities.
The model is not broadly available yet. This week, Google is opening access to a select group of cyber defenders, then expanding it in stages to a wider pool of approved partners via its Fairwind Program.
Fairwind offers governments, critical infrastructure operators and major technology platforms early access to advanced models for cyber defense. The company says more than 650 organizations currently participate.
Carbon follows Gemini 4 Argon, which Google launched two weeks ago. Some Fairwind partners already have exclusive access to Argon’s cybersecurity defense capabilities.
Google said Carbon scored 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, which tests a model’s ability to uncover flaws in real-world software. It also achieved 54.8% on the ExploitGym exploitation benchmark and 71.0% on Collinear’s CWE-bench patching benchmark, topping OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1 in the company’s comparison.
These results were obtained with no guardrails in place, the company noted.
Google frames exploitation as a defensive step that helps teams decide what to fix. “To prioritize which vulnerabilities to remediate first or remediate at all, cyber defenders increasingly rely on models to check which vulnerabilities are exploitable,” the company said.

Interswitch, a Nigerian payments technology company, says consumer education is the biggest hurdle to making tap-to-pay a mainstream payment method in Nigeria, even as banks and merchants prepare to support it. Speaking at Moonshot 2026 in Lagos on Thursday, Tomi Ogunlesi, divisional head of brands, communication, content and CSR at Interswitch, said the industry must convince consumers that tapping their cards or phones to pay is secure and convenient.
“The banks are ready,” Ogunlesi said. “Where more of the work needs to be done now, from our perspective as an industry, is on the merchant side and on the consumer side, but most on the consumer side.”
His comments come after Mastercard and Interswitch announced the launch of Google Pay in Nigeria, allowing eligible Mastercard holders to add their cards to Google Wallet and pay with compatible Android phones at contactless-enabled terminals. Interswitch’ said that it was working with five Nigerian banks, including GTBank, Wema Bank, ProvidusUnity Bank, Zenith Bank, and FirstBank, to expand tokenised tap-to-pay transactions. The company said it is also working to bring more merchants into the network, including supermarket chain, Spar, had shown interest.
Contactless payments are not new to Nigeria. In 2015, Unified Payments launched PayAttitude, an NFC-based payment service, with several Nigerian banks. It used a chip-enabled tag attached to a mobile phone or another surface to make payments at compatible terminals.

articles.title: Microsoft fixes Remote Desktop failures caused by recent Windows updates
articles.summary:
Microsoft has resolved a known issue that prevents non-admin users from connecting to devices via Remote Desktop when the "Administrator protection" security feature is enabled.
When Administrator protection is enabled, it prompts standard users to authenticate with Windows Hello (PIN or biometric) when they try to change the Windows Registry or install new apps.
This feature began rolling out in October 2025 and is now enabled by default in organizations using Windows security baselines after installing the October 2026 Windows security update.
Microsoft acknowledged on October 13 that Remote Desktop connections may fail with error 0xC000000D after installing the KB5124010 September 2026 non-security preview update (or Windows updates released since then) on systems running Windows 11 24H2 and later.
"This issue primarily affects enterprise-managed remote devices used as Remote Desktop hosts with Administrator protection enabled, regardless of how the feature was enabled," it said.
Remote Desktop connection failures now fixed
On Wednesday, Microsoft confirmed that this issue is fixed for users who installed this month's KB5127936 preview update.
"This issue was resolved by Windows updates released October 28, 2026 (KB5127936), and later," it noted. "We recommend you install the latest security update for your device as it contains important improvements and issue resolutions, including this one."

Kojima Productions a choisi une histoire inédite pour Death Stranding Isolations, portée par de nouveaux personnages, plutôt que de raconter à nouveau les aventures de Sam Porter Bridges. La série abandonne la 3D des jeux pour une animation dessinée à la main, confiée au studio japonais E&H production. Un pari audacieux avec un résultat de toute beauté.
Une Amérique reconnectée mais plus brisée que jamais dans Death Stranding Isolations
« Ma mère est devenue un cratère. » La phrase ouvre le synopsis officiel de Death Stranding Isolations et figure sur sa première affiche. Le récit prend place en Amérique du Nord, juste après que Sam a fini de raccorder le continent via le Réseau Chiral. Alors que l’Amérique renaît de ses cendres, ces nouveaux liens ont des conséquences que personne n’avait prévues.
Au cœur de ce paysage chaotique, nous suivons le destin croisé de plusieurs âmes perdues : un vieux sage qui connecte les survivants par des méthodes défiant toute logique, une soldate piégée dans un cycle de guerre sans fin, un jeune homme rongé par la rage… et surtout une jeune fille. Contrainte à l’isolement après la catastrophe, elle a fini par préférer la solitude et par couper tous ses liens avec le monde extérieur. Des rencontres de hasard vont la projeter dans un monde qu’elle ne reconnaît pas.

articles.title: Scaling Autonomous Root Cause Analysis For Regression Triage
articles.summary:
Solving difficult bugs while intelligently deciding what to investigate, what to rerun, and where to spend compute.
As semiconductor designs grow larger and more complex, debugging is becoming increasingly difficult to scale.
At DVCon earlier this year, Nvidia’s Stuart Oberman described first-silicon success as approaching a “statistical impossibility.” Semiconductor Engineering cites that debugging accounts for 44% of verification effort; a number reported in 2018, before the scale and complexity of today’s designs.
As designs get larger and design spaces are expanding, engineers are working across systems containing millions of gates. If design complexity continues to scale, debugging needs a fundamentally different approach. In this article, we will explain an AI-native approach to root cause analysis (RCA) and regression triage.
There are two important ways that debugging effort scales.
The first is bug difficulty.
Some bugs require deep tracing across design hierarchies, long pipelines, large waveforms, and multiple interacting components before the actual root cause becomes clear.
ChipAgents RCA was designed specifically for this axis. Rather than treating debugging as a simple question-answering problem, the system approaches RCA as a search problem. It explores high-probability traces, executes across different hypotheses, ranks the resulting explanations, and provides confidence scores to the engineer.

articles.title: Cloudflare Introduces Web Search API for AI Applications
articles.summary:
Cloudflare has recently launched a beta Web Search API through AI Gateway. Available through REST APIs and Cloudflare Workers, it provides unified logging, access controls, and billing, and supports bring-your-own-provider keys.
The API enables AI agents to retrieve live web results from Ceramic.ai, Exa, and Linkup. It provides a unified interface, integrates search billing with AI Gateway, logs search requests alongside model inference, and requires providers to follow verified-bot requirements and return source links.
Cloudflare’s Web Search API allows AI applications to retrieve current web content, including recent news, API changes, and technical documentation, and provide the results as context to language models during inference. Michelle Chen, group product manager at Cloudflare, Sam Else, senior director at Cloudflare, and Gabriel Massadas, senior systems engineer at Cloudflare, explain the challenge that the company is trying to address:
When you use an agent and it needs to fetch a live web page, the agent usually just guesses the URL of the page and then makes a tool call to curl it. This is why you’ll sometimes see web fetches come back with a 404 Not Found, which happens if the agent incorrectly guesses the URL of that information. As you can imagine, it’s not super efficient to randomly guess URLs all the time.

articles.title: Philadelphia’s Academy of Natural Sciences just closed – a blow for budding young scientists like me
articles.summary:
When I was a freshman in college at Villanova University outside Philadelphia, I visited the Academy of Natural Sciences for the first time.
My friends who were Philly natives were my tour guides, and I was inspired by their passion for the exhibits. I listened not only to the facts they shared about the museum, but also their childhood stories surrounding it.
As a kid, I remember going to the American Museum of Natural History in New York City and looking up at the massive dinosaur displays. I wondered how creatures as big as those used to walk the same ground as me. My favorite exhibit was the Hall of Ocean Life, where behind the staircase you see a dark, unlit diorama of a giant squid attached to a sperm whale.
The museum gave my curiosity a place to grow.
Now, as a Ph.D. student in physics, I research black holes, with the goal of one day becoming a professor and mentoring students. I was shocked when I heard the news that the Academy of Natural Sciences would be closing.
Over 200 years of hands-on science
Founded in 1812, the Academy of Natural Sciences in Philadelphia is the country’s oldest natural science museum. For two centuries, it has played a vital role in scientific research, education and public engagement. The academy’s research centered heavily on biodiversity, evolution, paleontology and environmental science. In 2011, Drexel University acquired the academy and manages its endowment.
The academy had offered a range of experiences, from the Dinosaur Hall to i…

Seitdem können Gruppenadmins und -mitglieder Neuankömmlingen in Whatsapp-Gruppenchats einen gewissen Teil des bisherigen Nachrichtenverlaufs zuschicken, damit diese auf dem Laufenden sind.

articles.title: Wikipedia’s operator says a bad AI copyright ruling could threaten the open web
articles.summary:
The Wikimedia Foundation is staking out a middle ground in a group of landmark AI copyright cases, pushing courts to legally protect large language models (LLMs) training on copyrighted work — but not chatbots regurgitating that work to users. An overly black-and-white ruling, it says, could either deprive Wikipedians of useful AI-based tools or endanger the open web.
Wikipedia’s operator says a bad AI copyright ruling could threaten the open web
In the NYT’s case against OpenAI, the Wikimedia Foundation says training AI should be fair use — but regurgitating articles shouldn’t.
In an amicus brief filed Friday, the nonprofit behind Wikipedia weighed in on a set of lawsuits pitting publishers including The New York Times against OpenAI and Microsoft, taking neither side. “Wikimedia is concerned that the parties’ positions in this case push for overbroad and simplified applications of the fair use doctrine” around AI, the organization says in its legal filing. A nuance-free victory for publishers, it fears, could let copyright holders “gatekeep” even innovative and transformative uses of their work. On the other hand, a victory for AI companies could constitute “a green light to snub licensing terms and fragment the flow of knowledge between human authors and audiences.”

articles.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings acquires ADT | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Thrive Holdings has acquired physical security company ADT for $10 per share or about $7.6 billion in equity, the companies announced on Thursday. Beyond equity, the total enterprise value of the deal is $15.3 billion, ADT said.
Thrive Holdings is the holding company spinout from Josh Kushner’s powerhouse VC firm Thrive Capital. It also counts OpenAI as its partner, as well as an investor. The firm’s mission is to hold other companies long-term, revitalizing them with AI. Currently, Thrive Holdings holds over 75 companies, it says.
As a partner, OpenAI supplies AI models and tech as well as people, otherwise known as forward-deployed engineers, to Thrive’s companies.
Neither ADT nor Thrive announced what new AI-powered security products they will be releasing, but they did tease that the plan was to invest and release new products. “ADT will form the foundation of Thrive Holdings’ smart home security business,” the press release said.
AI-powered physical security is having a moment right now. Apple just entered the field with a new line of smart home and home security products in collaboration with LG and Schneider Electric. Amazon updated its smart home line, including new AI-powered home cameras. ADT already partners with Apple and Google and is expected to continue to do so. And who knows what the future might bring? Some startups are offering AI dog robots as roving security guards.

There isn’t enough data on factory work, and there won’t be internet-scale data, the kind LLMs were built on, for robots for a long time. Our methodology means we can do more with less.”

articles.title: When Risk Becomes Personal: What Security Leaders Can Learn From a Cancer Diagnosis
articles.summary:
Risk management leaders educate people on measuring exposure, testing assumptions and advising on how best to prepare for incidents they hope won’t occur. They know that the absence of a security alert does not stand for safety; that resilience depends on preparedness, and that a plan is only as good as the people who can execute it.
But when the risk is personal, those ideas take on a heavier meaning.
Receiving a Cancer Diagnosis
I was diagnosed after a routine physical that included a PSA blood test. I had not noticed any symptoms and had no known family history. That raised a few eyebrows and ultimately, a stage-three prostate cancer diagnosis.
My experience is not a case for making a personal health choice or offering clinical advice. That’s far from my wheelhouse. However, it is a helpful framework for a profession that often talks about preparedness, leadership and resilience, but sometimes forgets to consider the people expected to deliver all three.
Risk Appetite Changes When the Asset is You
In professional life, leaders can be admirably objective. They can challenge a security control, decide whether a certain risk falls within an agreed tolerance, and explain to a board why a difficult trade-off is necessary. They are typically analyzing a faceless enterprise.
Risk management is more than recommending a set of analytical frameworks. It is also decision making under duress, usually done with incomplete information and nervous tempers. Leaders who never acknowledge t…

articles.title: Datadog Builds a Specialist AI Model for SRE Investigations
articles.summary:
Datadog has released Scout, a model trained to investigate production problems. It runs inside Bits Investigation, the company's AI SRE product, where it can pick up an alert, look through telemetry and suggest what caused the problem. Datadog engineers and a small number of customers are using it in a closed preview.
Most of the work described in the announcement concerns cost. An investigation may require many model calls as Bits tries a query, studies the result and decides what to check next. General-purpose models can do this, but Datadog says the bill makes it difficult to run them against every alert. The authors of the announcement want Bits to begin work while an engineer is still responding to the page.
"Our goal is for Bits to serve as an always-on first responder, gathering evidence and identifying likely causes before an engineer steps in."
Othmane Abou-Amal, Ben Cohen, Afshin Rostamizadeh, Ameet Talwalkar, Omri Sass and Daniel Shan
On Datadog's AlertEval benchmark, Scout medium received a similar score to GPT-6.1 Sol high and Claude Opus 5.5 high. Its estimated inference cost was between three and eight times lower. At the xhigh setting, Datadog says Scout matched Claude Fable 5.1 xhigh for one quarter of the cost. No prices are published, so these figures are relative to the cost of a Scout medium investigation.

articles.summary:
AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

articles.title: Unlocking Tensor Core Performance for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Atomistic simulations help researchers understand how molecules and materials behave, from chemical reactions and phase transitions to mechanical failure. These simulations come with a cost-accuracy trade-off. Quantum-mechanical methods such as density functional theory (DFT) can provide accurate energies and forces, but their computational cost often limits their use for large systems or long simulations. Classical interatomic potentials are much faster, but their fixed functional forms limit accuracy and generalizability across different atomic environments. Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) help bridge this gap. They use neural networks to predict potential energies and interatomic forces at a fraction of the cost, enabling researchers to study larger systems and longer timescales while retaining much of the required accuracy.
Running an MLIP efficiently, however, presents its own challenge. Atomistic simulations are sensitive to small errors that can accumulate over time and are most visible when computing forces, which are obtained by differentiating the predicted energy. During molecular dynamics simulations, these forces guide updates to atomic velocities and positions over many timesteps, making numerical precision important not only for physical accuracy but also for the stability of the resulting trajectory.
For this reason, many MLIPs continue to run inference in FP32, even though modern NVIDIA GPUs offer substantially higher matrix-multiplication thr…

articles.title: Rendre la vue aux aveugles : Elon Musk affirme que son implant cérébral est « prêt »
articles.summary:
Permettre à des personnes aveugles de voir grâce à un implant dans le cerveau : c’est l’un des projets de Neuralink, l’entreprise cofondée par Elon Musk. Et à en croire le milliardaire, le dispositif aurait franchi une étape importante. Dans une publication sur X le 30 octobre 2026, il affirme que Blindsight est « prêt sur le plan technique » et attend une autorisation réglementaire. Il réaffirme que cet implant doit permettre de voir à des personnes totalement aveugles, y compris celles qui n’ont jamais vu.
Dans un autre message publié sur X, le patron annonce aussi la prochaine étape de Telepathy, le dispositif de Neuralink déjà testé pour contrôler un ordinateur par la pensée. Selon lui, il permettra de communiquer plus vite qu’en parlant ou en tapant au clavier d’ici à quelques années.
Comment Blindsight pourrait-il rendre la vue ?
Pour comprendre le principe, il faut revenir au fonctionnement de la vision. La rétine, au fond de l’œil, transforme la lumière en signaux électriques. Ces informations sont ensuite transmises au cerveau, qui les interprète. Une maladie ou une blessure touchant les yeux ou les nerfs optiques peut interrompre ce trajet.
Blindsight doit contourner cette difficulté. Une caméra filme l’environnement, puis le dispositif transmet les informations à un implant chargé de stimuler les régions du cerveau impliquées dans la vision. L’objectif n’est donc pas de réparer les yeux, mais de produire des perceptions visuelles en passant directement par le cerve…

articles.summary:
Pour le Black Friday, Proton baisse fortement le prix de sa messagerie chiffrée : -60 % sur Proton Mail Plus et -50 % sur Proton Unlimited avec l’abonnement d’un an. Si vous hésitiez à quitter Gmail, c’est le moment.
Pour la plupart d’entre nous, Gmail est la boîte mail par défaut. Elle est gratuite, pratique, déjà installée sur le téléphone, et on n’y pense plus. Pourtant, elle contient une bonne partie de notre vie : factures, échanges avec la banque, documents administratifs, conversations privées, comptes en ligne. Tout cela est hébergé chez une entreprise dont le modèle économique repose sur la publicité.
Proton Mail propose l’inverse : une messagerie chiffrée, hébergée en Suisse, sans aucune publicité, financée uniquement par ses abonnés. Son principal frein était le prix. Jusqu’au 30 novembre, ce frein disparaît presque.
Gmail : gratuit, mais à quel prix ?
Gmail n’est pas gratuit, on le paie autrement. Google a bâti son modèle sur la publicité, et votre boîte mail en fait partie : des annonces s’affichent dans l’onglet Promotions, et vos usages enrichissent l’écosystème Google dans son ensemble. Avec l’arrivée de Gemini dans Gmail, l’IA lit désormais vos messages pour les résumer, proposer des réponses et faire des recherches dedans.
Il faut aussi tenir compte de la juridiction. Google est une entreprise américaine, soumise au Cloud Act, ce qui permet aux autorités des États-Unis de demander l’accès à des données même lorsqu’elles sont stockées en Europe. Pour une boît…

articles.title: Chrome extensions with 13.4 million installs caught hijacking searches
articles.summary:
A massive search-hijacking campaign involving 319 Chrome extensions with a combined 13.4 million reported installations redirected users' searches through tracking servers to generate advertising revenue from Bing and Yahoo.
A new report by Socket's John Tuckner expands on the researcher's April 2025 discovery of 57 Chrome extensions with 6 million users, adding 264 newly identified add-ons with another 8.7 million users.
"These extensions were created by a handful of organized operators all working from the same idea: quietly take over the browser's default search engine, route every query through a suspicious proxy server, and collect partner referral payments from Yahoo or Bing under a syndication partner ID," explained Tuckner.
The extensions, with the full list shared at the bottom of Socket's report, pretend to be PDF converters, manual finders, safe search, and AI search tools. However, for the most part, the extensions simply redirect users' searches through a series of sites until they land on Bing or Yahoo.
Although they are hosted on the Chrome Web Store, Google's official portal for Chrome add-ons, Socket says they are unlisted and don't appear in users' searches on the extension store.
Instead, the extensions are promoted through shady advertisements found on websites.
Tuckner explains that many of these extensions need almost no code to achieve their goal, as Chrome's built-in 'chrome_settings_overrides' setting allows them to replace the default search provider…

articles.title: From Functional Monitoring To In-System Test: Extending Voltage-Aware Observability
articles.summary:
Separate false failures caused by voltage droop from real structural defects.
By Aakash Jani, Henrique Mendes, and Robert Wilcox
In a previous blog, we highlighted the importance of combining physical and functional sensors to plan for new workloads. This use case remains relevant for high-performance AI and HPC systems because ‘spiky’ workloads induce severe droops that dominate power budgets.
Your $1 billion ASIC just had a scan failure during an In-System Test. How can you tell whether the failure is an actual structural failure, or one caused by physical phenomena like voltage droop? Scan patterns can often generate intense switching activity when long or multiple chains are toggled, which may induce a voltage droop. If the failure is due to a voltage droop, you have a few options: slow the shift clock, raise the voltage, or repartition your scan patterns. Without physical sensors that report conditions during the test, teams can’t tell the two cases apart and might throw away good parts on false failures.
Co-mingling physical and functional sensors is necessary across the system lifecycle because functional and physical failures are connected. Let’s move further down the system lifecycle into silicon deployment for another example.

articles.title: Anthropic Says Nobody Needs a Mental Model of Claude Code. Practitioners Are Testing That
articles.summary:
Anthropic has published how the Claude Code team runs code review now that Claude writes about 90% of Claude Code itself. The claim drawing the most scrutiny is not the percentage but what the team says it no longer needs.
The post, by Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt and Qing Wang, is the companion to Anthropic’s account of replacing git with an in-house system after its monorepo went from roughly 2,500 merged changes a day in May to more than 30,000 in September. Review was the next thing to break. The target is that most pull requests "merge with at most one human in the loop, who can be the author, with no increase in reverts or incidents."
On comprehension, the team is explicit:
Nobody on the team keeps a complete mental model of Claude Code in their head, and we don’t think anyone needs to. When someone wants to understand a part of the codebase, they ask Claude to write an explainer for exactly that slice. It takes minutes and reflects the code as it is today.
That passage dominated the Hacker News discussion, where commenter jonahx set out what it trades away:
There is no longer anyone to turn to if this system breaks by, eg, having a critical bug that no one can figure out. No causal model in anyone’s head that can be appealed to, to slowly and methodically debug. The new trust model is: We trust Claude to always understand the system enough to debug anything or make any reasonable change we could want.

Accelerate agentic AI with NVIDIA Nemotron models on Amazon EKS and SageMaker HyperPod EKS
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL joins the NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano, Nano Omni, Super, Ultra, and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning models already available on AWS. It’s a 120B-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model that activates 12B parameters per token. About Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open multimodal model distilled from Nemotron 3 Ultra. NVIDIA publishes the weights, training datasets, and post-training recipes, so you can customize the model for domain-specific workloads and run it on infrastructure you control. Model details:
- 120B total parameters, 12B active per token.
- Hybrid Mamba-2, MoE, and attention layers with a RADIO vision encoder.
- Context length up to 1M tokens.
- Input: text, image, document, and video.
- Output: text.
- BF16 and NVFP4 checkpoints.

IA amplia o controle das companhias sobre as tarifas

An AI agent given autonomy to run code will inevitably run code no human has reviewed. It may install model-selected packages, run scripts generated moments earlier, and iterate until a developer’s test passes; that risk is limited to a laptop. For a company, it can extend beyond the agent’s workload to any workload deployed on shared Kubernetes infrastructure. Cluster configurations can limit a container’s system calls, but an allowed call that reaches a kernel vulnerability can still expose the underlying node.
As agents proliferate, this gap has shifted workload isolation from a niche hardening requirement to a baseline need for platforms that run agents. This is a challenge our users at Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) have asked us to help solve.

Platform teams can assemble the stack rather than reinvent it, while native provider support simplifies configuration and maintenance. Managed Kubernetes services offer sandboxed pods this way, but runtimes isolate agentic workloads differently.

articles.summary:
A newly identified advanced persistent threat (APT) group tracked as UAT-11473 was observed exploiting CVE-2026-20127, an authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controllers, to deploy a custom malware framework called KeyDrift.
CVE-2026-20127 is a max-severity flaw that Cisco patched in February 2026, which allows remote attackers to gain privileged access to Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager and add rogue peers.
UAT-8616 has exploited the vulnerability as a zero-day since at least 2023, and recent research also linked its exploitation to the Chinese Volt Typhoon state-sponsored hacking group.
According to Cisco Talos researchers who reported on the activity, the UAT-11473 threat cluster appears to overlap with Volt Typhoon’s "Silent Train" covert access network, but they made no definitive links.

articles.title: Google Adopts DPoP to Strengthen OAuth 2.0 Against Token Theft and Replay Attacks
articles.summary:
Google's OAuth Platform has recently introduces support for Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession (DPoP), an OAuth 2.0 security mechanism designed to mitigate token theft and replay attacks.
Traditional OAuth bearer tokens operate on a "finders-keepers" model, making them vulnerable to Infostealer malware (e.g. RedLine, NodeStealer) and Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) attacks.
To prevent this types of attacks, DPoP uses cryptography to bind tokens to an asymmetric key pair generated by the client. Consequently, a stolen token cannot be replayed without the corresponding private key, which remains under the client’s control.
Google OAuth platform supports DPoP only for refresh tokens, while access tokens, which are shorter-lived, remain standard Bearer tokens. This decision is motivated by the fact that long-lived refresh tokens are "the primary vector for persistent online impersonation", whereas applying DPoP to access tokens would introduce "asymmetric cryptographic verification overhead" for each request.
It is worth noting that adopting DPoP adds several client-side requirements, including generating cryptographic keys, handling timestamps and nonces correctly, generating the appropriate HTTP headers and the required DPoP proof JWTs.
While DPoP provides protection for API tokens, it does not protect standard web application session cookies, which remain vulnerable to Infostealer malware. To address the threat of cookie theft, Google and the Web Incubator Community Group (WICG)…

An unprecedented leak of Department of Homeland Security records has exposed details of more than 41,000 employees or contractors who work for the department and its constituent agencies. The records include email addresses, phone numbers, and office addresses, but also references to internal systems and sensitive information on undercover and surveillance programs. In all, the leak provides a map of how DHS is organized and how it operates.
The records, which span DHS itself as well as seven component agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement and US Customs and Border Protection, were last updated on August 19, 2026. The transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets and cybersecurity researcher and journalist maia arson crimew previewed the data for WIRED, which they say they obtained from a group calling itself the Department of Peace.
DDoSecrets published the archive, which it calls “Icepick,” on Wednesday. In a press release, DDoSecrets says the data is from DHS’s Okta login system. In a note with the files, the hackers wrote, “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs.”
An Okta spokesperson tells WIRED that it is unaware of any breach of its systems. “We are aware of this report. Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised,” the spokesperson says.
The leak comes as DHS has aggressively pursued its critics, seeking to unmask anonymous social media users, obtain customer records on protesters, and…

articles.title: Rivian expands joint venture with VW to include AI assistant | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The $5.8 billion joint venture between Rivian and Volkswagen Group is expanding to include AI assistants.
Rivian is now licensing elements of its AI voice assistant technology to Volkswagen Group as part of the broader joint venture, according to the company’s third-quarter investor presentation released Thursday.
Rivian didn’t disclose the licensing fees, payment terms, or which Volkswagen vehicles will use the technology. However, the AI assistant, which recently rolled out to Rivian vehicles, could make its Volkswagen debut in the automaker’s low-cost EV called the ID EVERY1. The small four-door hatchback is slated to be the first VW vehicle to use Rivian’s software and electrical architecture under the joint venture established in 2024.
The joint venture between Rivian and VW Group has already expanded once before, at least financially. The companies initially announced a joint venture valued up to $5 billion, but within months VW upped its commitment to invest up to $5.8 billion in Rivian by 2027. The initial tie-up, formalized through an independent company that kicked off in November 2024, focused on bringing Rivian’s electrical architecture and software to Volkswagen’s next generation of vehicles.
Rivian described the expansion to include elements of its AI assistant technology as “a proof point for the extensibility of the platform we’ve built in-house.”

articles.title: TeamViewer Flaw Could Let Malicious Hosts Take Over Support Technicians’ Machines
articles.summary:
A high-severity vulnerability in the popular remote-access tool TeamViewer could be exploited to take over a viewer’s (an IT support technician’s) system, cybersecurity firm Remedio warns.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111585 (CVSS score of 8.8), the flaw is described as an integer overflow affecting the remote-control screen processing component of TeamViewer clients across Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.
Successful exploitation of the security defect could allow attackers to crash the viewer’s TeamViewer or execute arbitrary code on their system.
“Exploitation requires a user to establish a remote-control session to an attacker-controlled or compromised host,” TeamViewer notes in its advisory.
The issue, Remedio says, is rooted in how the host’s screen dimension is transmitted and used in the viewer: the host announces the geometry of the screen and the viewer uses the received dimensions to allocate an in-memory pixel buffer it then uses to decompress incoming screen updates.
This decode surface is only used if a hardware video decoder is not available for the session, but the host may refuse to negotiate the video codecs, thus forcing the viewer to that path.
A host can request a surface larger than what a screen can reach, and the path accepts it. An example would be 32768 by 32768 pixels at 32 bits per pixel, which overflows 32 bits, with every row past 31 being written out of bounds.

articles.title: Paula, española trabajando en Holanda: “Puedo decir que ahorro entre 800 y 1.100 euros todos los meses”
articles.summary:
Paula, una ciudadana española que lleva cerca de dos años viviendo en Holanda, ahorra “entre 800 el mes que menos gano y 1.000 o 1.100 el mes que más gano”, pagando un alquiler de unos 2.000 euros al mes, agua y electricidad incluidos, de los que su parte es de 1.000 euros. “Sí que es verdad que es caro”, admite; la dificultad para encontrar alojamiento se debe a que, en sus palabras, “La demanda aquí en Holanda es muy grande y hay muy poca oferta”, lo que hace que los precios estén, a su juicio, “un poco desorbitados”.

Su otro gasto regular es el gimnasio, con 38 euros, y la línea telefónica con datos ilimitados a cambio de una promoción para menores de 30 años, con 25 euros. Paula y su novio (con quien comparte vivienda) tienen una cuenta conjunta en la que ingresan 150 euros cada uno para la compra, pero su gasto medio en comida (tanto de ella como del novio) es de 300-350 euros al mes.
Se desplazan en un coche compartido que funciona con gas, pero consume gasolina, un gasto de 80 euros al mes, de los que se le reembolsa parte a Paula por kilómetros recorridos por su empresa. articles.title: Winzig, aber heikel: Nasa-Rover Perseverance entdeckt ultrafeine Staubpartikel auf dem Mars
articles.summary:
Gefahr für Astronauten? Nasa-Rover Perseverance entdeckt ultrafeine Staubpartikel auf dem Mars
Über 1645 Marstage hinweg hat der Nasa-Rover Perseverance feine und ultrafeine Marsstaubpartikel gemessen, die sich auf mitgeführten Proben von Raumanzugmaterialien abgesetzt hatten. Einige dieser Partikel sind theoretisch klein genug, um tief in die Lunge vorzudringen und womöglich sogar in den Blutkreislauf überzugehen. Jetzt wurden die Ergebnisse in den Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences veröffentlicht.
Feine und ultrafeine Partikel
Frühere Messungen erfassten Marsstaubpartikel mit einem Durchmesser von bis zu etwa 3 Mikrometern. Das „Planetary Instrument for X-ray Lithochemistry“ (PIXL) an Bord von Perseverance wies jetzt zwei noch kleinere Partikelklassen nach: feine Partikel mit einer Größe von 2,5 Mikrometern und ultrafeine, etwa 100 Nanometer große – oder wohl eher kleine – Partikel. Zum Vergleich: Die ultrafeinen Partikel sind rund 700-mal dünner als ein menschliches Haar. Die PIXL-Ergebnisse sind die ersten Vor-Ort-Messungen von feinen und ultrafeinen Partikeln auf dem Mars.
Welcher Stoff hält den Marsstaub besser ab?
Die winzigen Partikel könnten tief in die Lunge von Astronaut:innen vordringen, in den Blutkreislauf übertreten und unter Umständen lebenswichtige Organe beeinträchtigen. The scale of enterprise AI agents in deployment can range from thousands to millions of user interactions per day. Existing observability platforms make agentic traces easier for humans to monitor and inspect, but make it difficult to improve agent behavior at higher volumes.
Many teams end up sampling the top 1% or less of traces for manual review based on a particular metric, threshold or random selection, meaning that the vast majority of agent failures pass by.
“Aligning AI agents to human judgment is one of the biggest challenges of our time,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Julie Kheyfets (pictured, left). “Agents are incredible at attaining goals, but they lack access to the years of heuristics that we as humans have collected in our heads.”

articles.title: Build a repeatable PHP-to-Java migration engine with Kiro | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Build a repeatable PHP-to-Java migration engine with Kiro
When your team moves a mature PHP application to Java, you gain stronger type safety, broader library support, and more predictable scaling. A PHP codebase built over the years with Laravel, Symfony, or Doctrine carries business rules in places that are not obvious, from Eloquent traits to XML mapping files, so a structurally similar Java port can compile cleanly and still behave differently.
This post shows how to turn PHP-to-Java migration from a one-time leap of faith into a measurable, repeatable process using Kiro. Kiro is an AI integrated development environment (IDE) that pairs an AI agent with your codebase to run multi-step engineering tasks with you in the loop. The approach centers on a reusable engine: a shared methodology, a mechanical discovery scanner, and an eight-phase workflow. This engine treats the original PHP application as the specification and refuses to declare the Java port correct until a parity harness verifies it.

Before getting started, you need:
- Familiarity with PHP (Laravel/Eloquent or Symfony/Doctrine). Java knowledge (Spring Boot, JPA) helps you review the generated output, but the engine produces idiomatic Java for you, so you don’t need to rewrite the application in Java yourself.

articles.title: Why Kubernetes platforms keep rebuilding a layer they could share
articles.summary:
Why Kubernetes platforms keep rebuilding a layer they could share
Ask a platform team what they built last year, and the list likely includes a Kubernetes controller that creates a few objects in order and copies fields between them. No business logic, just wiring. A Deployment, a Service in front of it, and a ConfigMap whose one interesting value is the hostname the Service reports in its status. Kubebuilder turns building the first controller into a pleasant afternoon. The tenth brings its own reconcile bugs, upgrade path, and on-call rotation. It’s the same controller. It’s slightly different each time, and it exists in thousands of organizations.
Every ingredient, no recipe
Kubernetes has the ingredients: CRDs define new types. Controllers give them behavior. Server-side apply tracks who owns each field. CEL evaluates expressions, and OpenAPI schemas type every field. What Kubernetes does not provide is the recipe. Nothing says that several resources form one thing, or that a value in one comes from the status of another and must wait for it.

articles.summary:
GitHub says massive influx of AI-generated code required extra 4 million CPU cores and 160 petabytes of storage to manage — a sixfold increase to 7.4 billion monthly commits in one year
Everyone knew the rise was sharp, but the figures are staggering.
Is most programming code now made by AI? That's not hard to believe given the number of testimonies, but we now have exact figures behind that statement. GitHub, the world's largest code repository, says that over the course of this year, it added 4 million CPU cores, 160PB of storage, and 50 Tb/s of networking capacity to keep up with the influx of AI-generated code.
Raw repository activity saw a massive year-over-year increase, as per GitHub's technical report. Code commits (adding/removing code) grew sixfold, while merged pull requests (finalizing a feature or bugfix) jumped 4x.
The multipliers sound impressive enough, but the exponential growth pattern is even more so: half a year ago in April, there were already 1.4 billion commits per month — a figure that rose to 2.9 billion in August, and now sits at 7.4 billion for September. GitHub saw 17.9 billion code pushes in the past 12 months, which is more than all of 2024 and 2025 put together.

The researcher says the app drains wallets after unsuspecting users import their private keys into it.
Padre was a cryptocurrency trading platform, mainly used to buy and sell meme coins on Solana. It was later renamed Terminal by pump.fun, a platform focused on creating, buying, and selling cryptocurrency “meme coins” on the Solana blockchain.
Iris says the legitimate Padre trading service, now Terminal by pump.fun, is web-only, so any mobile apps impersonating it, including the one previously available on the App Store, are malicious.
At the time of BleepingComputer's initial investigation, we found two Padre apps on the App Store (ID 6802739263 and ID 6717572591). The former was the Iris-confirmed drainer app, while the latter is likely pump.fun's official app, live since October 2024.
The malicious Padre Terminal app has since been removed from the App Store, with its listing now returning a 404 error.
Iris told BleepingComputer it suspects the trading interface of the fake app is served remotely, but has not directly observed the wallet-draining screen.

This estimate, in the ministry’s October economic review, is slightly above the forecast of 7.1% by the Reserve Bank of India, released earlier this month. articles.title: Physics-Based Validation: The Foundation Of Trustworthy Agentic EDA
articles.summary:
What self-verifying agents validate their decisions against and why physics-based engines are the authority on correctness.
This is the third article in a series examining what it takes to build production-ready AI agents for EDA. The first explored the architectural decisions required for agents to operate reliably in production environments. The second examined what self-verifying means in an agentic EDA workflow: how agents continuously check their decisions as they work, rather than waiting until the end of a run.
But what exactly are those decisions being verified against?
The answer is physics. More specifically, the deterministic, physics-based EDA engines that define whether a design is correct. A self-verifying agent checks its own work, and a physics-validated workflow confirms that work is correct.
Chip design has always faced physics-based constraints. Every transistor, every wire, every timing path, and every thermal gradient is governed by the fixed laws of physics, regardless of how the design was created. This is why tapeout is binary: silicon either works or it does not.
When AI enters this domain, that physical reality does not change. The relevant question is not whether an AI system can reason about physics, but whether the outputs it produces have been confirmed by the engines that enforce that physics.
That distinction separates a model that is capable of reasoning about physics from a workflow that is physics-validated.

Materials engineering helps bridge the gap between advanced chip designs and what manufacturers can produce reliably at scale.

Security ratings company SecurityScorecard Inc. today released an open benchmark for testing whether artificial intelligence models can handle third-party risk management work without being turned against the companies using them.
The TPRM Benchmark is built for vendor risk programs, where a model may need to interpret security telemetry and decide which exposures matter. A lot of what the model reads comes from questionnaires and documents that vendors filled out themselves, and parts of that may be incomplete or manipulated on purpose. SecurityScorecard says generic benchmarks built around static or academic tasks were not designed with that in mind.
On the capability side, tasks cover disciplines such as exposure triage and fourth-party technology risk, and each one starts as a snapshot of SecurityScorecard’s own vendor-risk telemetry that domain experts check before any model is scored. articles.title: Our climate models have a big, dangerous blind spot
articles.summary:
Our climate models have a big, dangerous blind spot
A powerful feedback loop could drive more warming than predicted.
Climate change itself is increasingly fueling climate change. Rising concentrations of greenhouse gases are driving up global temperatures, setting off dangerous feedback loops that we have not fully accounted for in our climate models—or our emissions-reduction goals.
Scientists have long warned that warming would propel further warming in various ways, but a growing number of observations and studies are at last providing a sharper sense of just how powerful these cascading effects could be. And, by extension, they’re showing how much faster the planet may warm in this century.
A study in Environmental Research Letters in September, synthesizing the results of previous papers, found that the additional carbon dioxide and methane released from thawing permafrost, intensifying wildfires, hotter lakes and reservoirs, and wetter, warmer wetlands alone could drive global average temperatures up 0.2 °C to 0.4 °C this century. That would come on top of the 2.6°C of warming above preindustrial levels that modelers are already expecting through 2100. The additional heat could subject many of the world’s cities to monthslong heat waves and expose hundreds of millions of people to flooding.
None of the models that inform the major UN climate reports, which assess how much the planet will likely warm under various emissions scenarios, account for all these feedback effe…

Android 11, sorti en 2020, garde 10,5 % du parc. Fin 2021, il touchait presque un quart des appareils.

articles.title: Is It Getting Hot In Here? Why Thermal Is No Longer A Signoff Problem

Applying the appropriate level of simulation and abstraction at each stage of the design process is key to effective thermal analysis.
AI, high-performance computing and advanced semiconductor packaging have pushed power density higher, and that means managing heat is becoming one of the most consequential challenges in electronic design.
The issue is no longer simply how to cool a chip after it has been designed. Thermal behavior now affects decisions spanning device performance, package architecture, mechanical stress, reliability, floor planning and ultimately system performance. So engineering teams must shift thermal analysis to earlier in the design process as they consider a much broader multi-physics strategy.
Traditionally, engineers could isolate and analyze many physical effects separately. Electrical performance could be evaluated in one environment, thermal behavior in another and mechanical stress in another and so on. But with increasing integration, a change intended to improve performance in one domain can create unintended consequences elsewhere. Higher power can increase temperature; temperature can change electrical behavior; and thermal expansion can introduce mechanical stress that ultimately affects reliability.

articles.summary:
Scientists overcome a hidden obstacle to more powerful quantum computers
- Date:
- October 25, 2026
- Source:
- RIKEN
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a way to operate multiple silicon qubits simultaneously with remarkable accuracy, overcoming a major challenge in scaling up quantum computers. Their new technique maintained accuracy of approximately 99.9% even when all five qubits were running at once, opening the door to larger and more powerful quantum processors.
- Share:
Silicon spin qubits could play a major role in the future of quantum computing because they can be produced using the same semiconductor manufacturing methods that make today's computer chips. However, researchers have faced a significant challenge. When multiple silicon qubits are controlled at the same time, their operations tend to become less accurate. Building practical, large quantum computers will require scientists to control many qubits simultaneously while keeping errors to a minimum.
Researchers at the RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and their collaborators have now made important progress toward solving this problem. In a study published in Nature Physics, the team demonstrated highly accurate control of several silicon spin qubits operating simultaneously. Their experiments used an array of five qubits connected to a shared microwave control line. articles.title: Acabar con las llamadas spam parecía imposible, pero una herramienta desarrollada por Movistar lo está consiguiendo

El problema. A pesar de las medidas impuestas por el Gobierno, como el Plan Antiestafas Telefónicas, el registro de alias para los SMS o el prefijo 400, el spam continúa siendo constante (yo misma lo sufro cada dos por tres). Y eso ha obligado a los operadores a mover ficha.

El pasado mes de marzo, además, Movistar y O2 activaron la herramienta 'Llamadas molestas' para combatir las llamadas comerciales. Y ahora, está trabajando en una nueva funcionalidad que permitirá bloquear también los SMS fraudulentos.
Solución a nivel de red contra el fraude. Hasta hace poco, la tarea de combatir las llamadas comerciales y/o fraudulentas recaía exclusivamente en el usuario, pero eso ha cambiado en los últimos meses. Ahora, la red de telefonía (fija y móvil) es capaz de detectar, identificar y bloquear ese tipo de llamadas.

articles.title: Americans are losing enthusiasm for their jobs, with AI and remote workers at the center of the decline
articles.summary:
In a nutshell: Do you feel a lack of enthusiasm for your job, or struggle with motivation and focus at work? If you do, then you're in the majority. A recent poll of the US workforce found that employee engagement in Q3 fell to its lowest level since 2011. Much of the decline came from remote and hybrid employees across the country, especially those in organizations that have adopted AI.
Gallup began tracking employee engagement in 2000, when 26% of employees in the US said they were engaged. That figure stayed steady between 26% and 30% through 2013, then climbed to a peak of 36% in 2020.
But engagement has fallen since the start of the decade. It stood at 29% last quarter, the lowest level in 15 years. It's also two percentage points lower than the previous quarter.
Gallup writes that each percentage point in engagement represents approximately 1.6 million US employees. The Q3 decline is equivalent to about 3.2 million fewer engaged workers, bringing the total decrease since 2020 to approximately 11 million.
The decline reflected two aspects of employees' work experience: knowing what is expected of them and feeling cared about as a person.
Gallup says businesses should care more about their employees' morale, as disengaged workers can impact a firm's productivity, customer service, quality, safety and profitability.
Interestingly, employees' understanding of what was expected of them declined around twice as much among hybrid and fully remote workers. Jim Harter, chief sci…

articles.title: Un propietario aparca su moto junto a su coche en la misma plaza de garaje y los vecinos se quejan: la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal aclara los límites y si la comunidad le puede sancionar
articles.summary:
Seguro que no te resulta extraño ver cómo un coche y una moto comparten una plaza de garaje, aprovechando al máximo el espacio y dejando un margen mínimo para maniobrar. Y puede que alguna vez te hayas preguntado si eso realmente se puede hacer, porque una cosa es que los dos vehículos quepan y otra que puedan dejarse allí sin más.
La Ley de Propiedad Horizontal responde a esta duda: no prohíbe de forma general aparcar un coche y una moto en la misma plaza.
Pero sí hay matices respecto al espacio que ocupan. La moto puede tener las ruedas dentro de las líneas y, aun así, sobresalir. Lo esencial es que los dos vehículos deben quedar dentro de la plaza y dejar libres las zonas de paso, sin dificultar las maniobras de los demás. Si el vecino tiene que esquivar una moto que invade el pasillo para poder salir, ya hay un problema que reclamar.
El artículo 9.1 de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal obliga a respetar los elementos comunes y a actuar con diligencia en las relaciones con los otros propietarios. Eso exige que, en el caso de que queramos reclarmar como vecinos, debamos concretar el motivo de la queja ya que la mera presencia de dos vehículos no demuestra que se esté incumpliendo una norma.
La comunidad también puede aprobar reglas de convivencia y de uso de las zonas comunes, como recoge el artículo sexto de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal. Estas deben respetar la legislación y los estatutos. Ahora bien, la ley no establece una multa automática por aparcar juntos el coche y la…

articles.title: Enzi’s Oji Udezue Says Africa Needs Cheaper AI
articles.summary:
Africa’s ability to benefit from artificial intelligence will depend on bringing down the cost of using it, Oji Udezue, president of Enzi, told Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos.
Udezue said reducing the cost of inference, the process through which AI models generate responses and perform tasks, was essential to making the technology affordable for businesses and individuals across the continent.
“Our goal is to make AI cheaper for Africa and America,” he said. “The future of AI really goes through inference.”
His argument shifts attention from the race to build more powerful models to the economics of putting them to work. For businesses using AI to answer customer enquiries or support employees, the expense recurs each time the system performs a task. Those costs can determine whether a promising application becomes viable for everyday use.
Udezue highlighted the gap between the cost of using AI and what many Africans earn, warning that access to a tool means little if people cannot afford to use it consistently.
The distinction matters as companies seek to integrate AI into their operations. A service affordable for occasional queries may prove too expensive when used throughout the working day or offered to thousands of customers. Lower inference costs could make those applications more commercially practical.

articles.title: Floods, Fires and Blackouts: A Disaster Recovery Plan for a Business With One Server - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Understanding the Stakes for Small Businesses
Disasters strike without warning, and for businesses operating with a single server, the impact can be catastrophic. Floods, fires, and blackouts not only threaten physical infrastructure but also jeopardize critical data and operational continuity. According to a report by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), 40% to 60% of small businesses never reopen after a disaster. This alarming statistic highlights the importance of having a robust disaster recovery plan tailored to businesses with limited IT resources.
For small businesses with only one server, the stakes are even higher. Unlike larger companies with distributed systems and multiple data centers, a single-server setup represents a single point of failure. If that server goes down, the entire business can grind to a halt. This makes it critical to understand the risks and prepare accordingly with a comprehensive disaster recovery plan.
Why a Disaster Recovery Plan is Non-Negotiable
At the core of any disaster recovery strategy lies the ability to restore operations swiftly and efficiently. For a business with one server, downtime translates to total business interruption, loss of customer trust, and potential financial ruin. A disaster recovery plan is a documented, structured approach that ensures a business can recover data, maintain continuity, and resume normal operations after an incident.

articles.title: Japan Airlines suffers third-party data breach exposing passenger info
articles.summary:
Japan Airlines (JAL) has announced that a data breach at Amadeus’s Passenger Service System exposed the data of about 92,000 customers.
JAL Group, which operates the airlines JAL and Japan Transocean Air, uses the system to handle passenger reservations, ticketing, and check-in.
According to its announcement, Amadeus notified the airline on October 23, 2026, that unauthorized access to its systems occurred between August 10, 2023, and September 23, 2026.
As a result of this lengthy breach, the threat actor accessed reservation codes (PNRs), names, flight dates, routes, and travel classes for approximately 90,000 customers.
An additional 2,000 customers had the above data types exposed, plus their email addresses, phone numbers, passport numbers, nationalities, frequent flyer numbers, and flight, ticket, and seat numbers.
JAL says credit card numbers and passwords were not compromised, and assured that it currently has no evidence of customer information being misused.
The company said Amadeus has now implemented the necessary security measures and flight operations are unaffected.
Broader impact
Amadeus is an IT firm that provides solutions for travel agencies, airlines, airports, and hotels.
It is a major tech supplier to global aviation, used by over four hundred airlines, 210 airport operators, 34 cruise and ferry lines, and 2 million hotels.

articles.title: How Ghana’s TrustCheck helps shoppers vet online sellers before they pay - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
Ghanaian startup TrustCheck has built a review and trust platform that allows consumers to check out businesses, especially social media sellers, before they part with their money.
Launched in January of this year by Elliot Brenya, Tema-based TrustCheck lets users look up a business, read verified customer reviews, and see a trust score out of 100. The score combines a business’s rating, review volume, how responsive it is to customers, verification status and any open disputes.
“A lot of buying in Ghana now happens on Instagram, TikTok, X and WhatsApp. You see a product, message the seller, send money by Mobile Money and hope it arrives,” Brenya told Disrupt Africa. “Most of the time it does, but when it doesn’t, there is usually no way to get your money back and no record that warns the next person. TrustCheck is meant to be that record.”
Brenya was inspired to build the platform after being scammed while buying a mobile device, having relied on fake ratings for the vendor.
All reviews on TrustCheck are moderated before going live, and reviewers can attach proof of purchase, such as MoMo receipts or order chats, which only moderators can see. Businesses cannot pay to have reviews removed, but can claim their pages for free, respond to reviews and apply for verification. This month the startup also launched a scam check for phone numbers, MoMo numbers, social media handles and websites, as well as a public API that returns a business’s trust score.

articles.title: OPINION: You can’t scale with a startup mindset | EU-Startups
articles.summary:
The best advice once your company achieves product-market fit? Don’t get stuck on things that got you there, keep adjusting your architecture and workflow to fit your new realities and sizes.
Starting strong is one thing, but the real point is pushing past the growth ceiling without crashing: McKinsey found 78% of products launched successfully only to fail later on. Having worked in international expansion, I have seen how the practices that help a startup gain traction can cause troubles as it grows. Here is my top-5 of what’s better to be changed once a company is too big for a startup mode, and what habits are worth keeping in mind.
Money moves faster than decisions
Congratulations, it’s been your big funding round. Having more capital can feel like you have almost unlimited freedom to chase everything at once. This money mostly goes to ideas that already work, more on tests, all at once. In a ten-person startup, the founder knows every ongoing experiment. In a 100-person company, nobody does. Tests overlap, compete for the same target audience, and rarely get switched off. Meanwhile, decision-making slows down as more people have something to say. More money won’t fix messy operations, it just makes the mistakes more expensive.

AWS Elastic Beanstalk for regulated workloads: Built for the next decade, not just the first deploy
For more than a decade, the managed application platform industry has optimized around a compelling promise: get code running as quickly as possible.
Five-minute deployments. Git-based workflows. Minimal configuration. Infrastructure abstracted away from developers. That simplicity changed how software gets built, and for good reason. Application teams should spend more time building software and less time assembling infrastructure. But for organizations in regulated industries, getting an application running is only the beginning.
A patient scheduling system, financial application, government service, or aerospace workload may remain in production for years. During that time, operating systems need patching. Runtimes reach end of support. Security requirements evolve. Applications scale. Teams change. Auditors ask for evidence. Regulatory frameworks expand.
For these organizations, the question is no longer simply: How quickly can we deploy? It is: How easily can we deploy, and keep that application secure, supported, observable, auditable, and operational for years?
“The services built for fast starts also need to support long stays.”
That is why platform selection for regulated workloads runs on three axes rather than one. Developer simplicity still matters. But compliance posture and service continuity decide whether that simplicity survives an audit or a roadmap change.

articles.title: The Complexity Between The Bits
articles.summary:
What biological reasoning can teach us about verifying silicon systems.
By Vidya Chandran Darbari and Ashish Darbari
A recent conversation about carbon intelligence and silicon intelligence stayed with me. What interested me was not which one wins, but the complexity we take on as we ask silicon to sense, interpret, decide and act.
My work as an experimental structural biologist taught me to ask what a structure could explain, and what it could not. Solving a molecular structure was not the same as explaining the behaviour of the system to which it belonged. The next question was always about mechanism: what happens when the parts interact? That question shaped my perspective as a deep generalist in life sciences, connecting molecular mechanisms, biological networks and system behaviour.
Now, as Chief Strategy and Operations Officer at Axiomise, I return to that question in a different setting.
A chip is not a cell. But investigating biological complexity can sharpen how we investigate engineered systems—provided the comparison changes a question we ask, an observation we make or an obligation we verify. Otherwise, it remains an interesting analogy.
In life sciences, a protein interaction map is where questions begin. A connection identifies a possible interaction; it does not establish when that interaction matters. Concentration, localization, binding affinity, feedback and timing influence the outcome.

articles.title: Netflix Titus Adds Single-Tenant VM Isolation for Containers
articles.summary:
Netflix has added single-tenant Titus, a mode that runs one task alone on its own right-sized EC2 instance. The Compute/Platform team still owns and patches the host, so application teams keep the same API and deployment path. First adopters include stateful, high-throughput streaming workloads. Here, a neighbor's interference can lead to minutes of checkpoint recovery.
Titus launches millions of containers a week across tens of thousands of EC2 instances and is multi-tenant by default. Netflix says that cgroups, seccomp, the iocost controller, and traffic shaping can’t split shared hardware. This includes resources like the last-level cache and memory bandwidth. Its HTB traffic shaper also takes a global lock. A container that floods the host with small packets can burn the kernel CPU and starve its neighbors. Predictive CPU pinning and eBPF-based detection helped, but Netflix concluded that shared-kernel tuning narrows the gap without closing it.

articles.title: Turning a solar power system into its own backup
articles.summary:
Rather than directly converting photons into electricity, concentrated solar energy uses mirrors to turn sunlight into heat, which can then be used to drive traditional generating turbines. Up to about a decade ago, there was a case to be made that concentrated solar energy had a bright future, as improvements in heat storage had turned it into a way to generate power around the clock.
It wasn’t to be. While concentrated solar costs fell enough to compete with nuclear power, the price of photovoltaics plunged, making solar panels the cheapest source of power in most locations. Currently, if you have a good site to generate solar power, then the economics of PV panels are hard to beat.
That has left us needing to build a mixture of other facilities—typically batteries and natural gas facilities—to handle overnight needs or weather-driven shortfalls. But a small company is promising that it can help avoid the need to build a separate facility. Its version of concentrated solar is designed so that a fossil-fueled backup system shares most of the generating hardware with the solar side.
Back to the future?
Concentrated solar, also called solar thermal, is pretty simple in principle. Most of the site is covered with heliostats, devices that incorporate mirrors and a motorized tracking system that can keep their focus on a single point as the Sun moves across the sky. articles.title: Hugging Face malware campaign returns to hijack GPUs for crypto mining
articles.summary:
A cryptomining and backdoor campaign that abuses Hugging Face model repositories came back within days of being taken down.
Its most popular malicious model was downloaded more than 28,000 times.
Separately, researchers flagged a fake Solana starter kit on GitHub, live since late 2025, that is positioned to trick AI coding agents into installing a remote access trojan.
Code runs before the model loads
Researchers at Pluto Security found 31 malicious repositories across seven Hugging Face accounts, published in two waves since September.
The models pose as small Qwen2 test checkpoints. They target GPU hosts running self-hosted inference servers such as Xinference and GPUStack.
With linked models included, the repositories have more than 32,000 downloads. Pluto notes that this counts downloads, not confirmed infections.
Instead of using poisoned weights or pickle exploits, the campaign abuses a Hugging Face option, trust_remote_code, that lets a model ship its own Python code. When a user enables it, that code runs on their machine as soon as the model loads.
The most downloaded model, MENXIANGYU/qwen2-tiny, contained no actual model at all. Its code quietly installs a cryptocurrency miner disguised as a Linux system process, restarts it if killed, and removes competing miners from the machine.
Some versions also open a reverse shell, giving the attacker direct access to the infected server.

articles.title: Drupal Commerce Core Vulnerability Exploited Against Online Stores
articles.summary:
Drupal is urging online store owners to patch a highly critical access bypass vulnerability in the Commerce Core module, warning that it is being exploited in the wild.
Tracked as CVE-2026-118539, the issue affects a contributed module that adds e-commerce features to Drupal websites, including a shopping cart and checkout process. Drupal’s statistics show the module is used on more than 42,000 sites.
“The module doesn’t sufficiently protect certain routes and entity fields, leading to an access bypass that may financially impact the vendor,” Drupal explains in its advisory.
The Drupal security team gave the issue a risk score of 21 out of 25. According to the score, unauthenticated attackers can exploit the flaw no matter how the module is set up.
Drupal has confirmed the attacks but has not said how the bug is being exploited, who is behind the activity, or how many sites have been targeted. It has also not said whether the vulnerability was exploited as a zero-day, before patches became available.
The vulnerability affects 3.x versions before 3.3.13 and earlier releases before 8.x-2.41. Administrators should update to one of the two fixed versions and review their store orders.
“Sites should audit their orders for inconsistencies as this vulnerability is being actively exploited,” the advisory reads.
