articles.title: Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.
articles.summary:
Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.
Emerging evidence suggests some people with eating disorders are misusing weight-loss drugs.
GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are one of the biggest biotech breakthroughs of the last decade. But to some clinical psychologists, they can represent something more sinister—a potential trigger for eating disorders.
A new report suggests that the global incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa shot up between 1990 and 2023—by a whopping 71%. By 2023, there were an estimated 18.1 million people living with one of these two disorders.
What’s worse is that the number is likely to be much higher than that once we factor in other eating disorders. And, disturbingly, those in the field are already starting to see GLP-1 weight-loss drugs exacerbating the issue.
Cheri Levinson is a clinical psychologist at the University of Louisville in Kentucky who has specialized in eating disorders for almost 20 years. She says she’s now seeing more patients with more severe symptoms than at any other time in her career, and that many of them are misusing GLP-1s. “This is the worst I’ve seen things,” she says.
Eating disorders are mental health conditions in which people’s eating behaviors impact their health. They include anorexia nervosa (defined by a fear of weight gain), bulimia nervosa (in which people binge and purge), binge eating disorder, and others.

Breet, founded in 2019, converts cryptocurrency into cash for individuals in Nigeria and Ghana. It also offers an application programming interface that allows businesses to accept crypto payments and receive settlement in local currency.
The proposition separates the payment method from the currency a merchant ultimately wants to hold. Customers can pay with digital assets, while businesses receive local money without having to build a crypto operation of their own.
For Mbene, the objective is to reduce the work required to complete that transaction. “We’re just obsessed with simplicity,” she said.

articles.title: Cómo detectar estafas por voz: transferencias de dinero urgente e historias difíciles de confirmar
articles.summary:
Una llamada o un mensaje de voz por WhatsApp puede aparentar una emergencia familiar, un problema bancario o una solicitud laboral inesperada. Las estafas por voz buscan forzar transferencias de dinero o la entrega de datos sensibles antes de que la víctima pueda comprobar lo que ocurre.
El recurso de una voz conocida ya no alcanza para confirmar una identidad. Según ESET, la inteligencia artificial facilitó la imitación de voces y elevó la capacidad de persuasión de estas maniobras. Qué pasa si solicitan dinero con urgencia
El primer elemento suele ser la presión. Quien llama afirma que necesita dinero de inmediato por un accidente, una detención, un inconveniente durante un viaje o un supuesto bloqueo de una cuenta. El objetivo es reducir el tiempo disponible para evaluar la situación y llevar a que la persona actúe bajo miedo o preocupación.
Expertos aseguran que la solicitud puede incluir frases como “no cortes”, “no avises a nadie” o “hay que resolverlo ahora”. articles.title: Why MCP servers should tell agents what to do next
articles.summary:
Why MCP servers should tell agents what to do next
Many MCP servers do one thing. An agent asks for data, and the server hands it back. AWS’s James Ward thinks that leaves a lot on the table. The protocol works best, he told me, when the server acts less like a database and more like another voice in the conversation.
Ward is a principal developer advocate at AWS and sits on the technical committee of the Agentic AI Foundation, the Linux Foundation group that now houses MCP. I sat down with him last week at AGNTCon + MCPCon in San Jose the day before he and co-presenter Alexander Ioffe were set to give a session on moving MCP from a basic API to an agent integration interface.
“Many times our MCP servers are just these APIs, like ‘get me the customers,’ and that is a good place to start,” Ward said. “I imagine MCP as the third person in this conversation, or a fourth or a fifth, depending on how many MCP servers you have.”
In practice, that means a tool response carries guidance with the data. It tells the agent what it just did, what it might want to do next, and where to find more.
The other half of his pitch is visibility. Web developers can trace a click on a page all the way down to the database. “MCP by default doesn’t have any way to do trace ID,” Ward said.
The workaround AWS uses is rather low-tech. Add a session ID parameter to the tools and tell the agent to pass it on every call, so individual calls can be stitched into one journey. A second parameter can carry th…

Anthropic spent less than a third of its $8.9 billion first-half compute bill on serving customers, with most of the rest going into training, research, and running Claude internally, its S-1 filing shows. It has meanwhile signed up for hundreds of billions of dollars more in TPU and GPU capacity. By our math, it has meanwhile signed up for roughly $800 billion more in TPU and GPU capacity, and revenue per compute dollar jumped from $0.40 in Q1 2025 to $2.08 in Q2 2026, which the company links to capacity purchased 12–18 months ahead.
Anthropic’s IPO is likely to beat that of rival OpenAI, which filed confidentially before CEO Sam Altman said its own won’t come this year, amid widespread doubts about an AI bubble. Whether AI labs can cover what it costs to serve their models is an open question.
Anthropic appears to do so easily: it spent $2.4 billion serving customers in the first half of the year, versus $16.3 billion in revenue. Paying for what it has on order is more difficult. Cryptocurrency exchange Binance is investigating a potential security breach involving up to $5.8 billion in digital assets, in what could become the largest cryptocurrency hack in history.
If confirmed stolen, the amount would far exceed the $1.5 billion stolen from Bybit by North Korean hackers in February 2025, the largest confirmed crypto heist on record.
The suspected breach has already prompted stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle to freeze more than $2.3 billion in assets associated with the incident.
In a statement to BleepingComputer, a Binance spokesperson confirmed that the exchange was investigating reports of a potential security issue while reassuring customers that their funds were safe.
"Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating. Rest assured that user funds are completely safe," the spokesperson told BleepingComputer.
"Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information."
Binance also warned customers to remain cautious of scams and avoid unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.
Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) said on X that the incident appeared to be a hack, while noting that he no longer manages the exchange and expects all user funds to be fully covered.

With 1 trillion parameters and 52 billion active parameters, ML4 is natively multimodal and has received three additional weeks of reinforcement training and customer testing. Para OpenAI, la fidelidad no significa obedecer al pie de la letra. Implica entender lo que quieren y valoran la empresa, los desarrolladores y los usuarios, y actuar con criterio cuando esa comprensión es incompleta.

articles.title: Netflix Treats GPU Reliability as a Distributed Systems Problem
articles.summary:
Netflix has detailed how it is building a reliability platform for large-scale GPU training and inference, using layered health checks, automated remediation, and fault-tolerant training to keep jobs running despite hardware failures.
The problem is particularly acute for large AI training jobs. A model may run for weeks across hundreds of GPUs, with all workers operating in lockstep. A single failed GPU, degraded network adapter, or slow machine can therefore stop or significantly slow the entire workload. Netflix has built its GPU compute platform on Kubernetes and designed it to detect these failures, remove unhealthy capacity automatically, and allow long-running jobs to recover from machine loss.
The approach has produced measurable results: Netflix reports more than 99.95% GPU-node availability and an increase in job success from approximately 98% to more than 99.5%.
A conventional cloud health check can establish that a virtual machine is running and reachable, but that does not mean its GPUs are capable of running a distributed training workload.
Netflix found that a GPU can respond normally to a status query while failing once memory is allocated or sustained computation begins. Similarly, a network adapter may be present but have fewer links than expected, allowing collective operations to continue at severely reduced bandwidth.

articles.title: Fresh WordPress Vulnerability in Attackers’ Crosshairs
articles.summary:
Threat actors started exploiting a new high-severity WordPress vulnerability within hours of patches rolling out, Defiant warns.
Patched on October 28 in WordPress 7.1.4, the security defect impacts the WordPress update process and can be exploited for remote code execution.
According to Defiant, it is a race condition in WordPress’s Core update process that can be exploited without authentication. The attack complexity, however, is high. No CVE identifier has been assigned to the vulnerability yet.
The weakness stems from predictable, web-accessible staging paths during the upgrades. New files are unpacked into a predictable directory that is accessible from the web on many servers.
“The attacker needs a full-package update containing the installer files, public web and PHP access to the staging tree, a predictable or discovered staging path, and enough time to complete the attack before WordPress cleans up the temporary files,” Defiant explains.
According to the web security firm, threat actors are already attempting to exploit the vulnerability, polling the vulnerable paths repeatedly in their attempts to hit the seconds-long exploitability window.
While an attacker does not need an account on the site to exploit the flaw, they do need “to hit a very narrow window while WordPress is unpacking a complete Core update,” Defiant says.

articles.title: How Edge AI Helps Humanoid Robots React Faster Than a Central GPU - EE Times
articles.summary:
STMicroelectronics argued that humanoid robots should use onboard sensors and cameras to handle fast reactions on the robot, and leave only whole-body coordination to a central GPU, because a round trip to the GPU adds latency a moving robot cannot afford. The chipmaker is still weighing whether to build more powerful MCUs or MPUs for the task, a decision it says depends on how the robotics market develops.
“Every millisecond counts,” Allan Lagasca, director of STMicroelectronics’ robotics segment strategic program, told EE Times. “If you want a fast reaction, you should move the processing to the edge. If you want the entire system to work together, that is where the GPU comes in.”
Running inference closer to the task can reduce the workload sent to a central GPU and avoid delays associated with transferring data and returning commands, Lagasca said. In robotics, those delays can affect physical movement.
When two hands coordinate to transfer an object, for example, a delayed command can cause a joint to miss its target. Even if individual joints miss their targets by only a few millimeters, the combined movement can be affected.
“If inference is performed at the edge, the system can send the necessary command locally and respond faster,” he said.

articles.title: Passkeys Are Better Than Passwords. But They Are Not Enough.
articles.summary:
For decades, passwords have been one of cybersecurity’s most persistent weaknesses. Users forget them, reuse them, share them, and surrender them to convincing phishing sites. Attackers steal credentials, automate credential stuffing, and increasingly use artificial intelligence to make social engineering more effective.
What are passkeys?
Passkeys promise to eliminate much of this problem.
Built on public-key cryptography, passkeys replace shared secrets with cryptographic credentials. There is no password for an attacker to steal, intercept through phishing, or reuse against another service. Properly implemented passkeys are also phishing-resistant because authentication is bound to the legitimate service.
That represents a significant improvement over passwords and many traditional forms of multi-factor authentication (MFA). But it does not answer a more fundamental question: Just because someone successfully authenticated, should we continue to trust that identity?
Passkeys strengthen authentication. They do not eliminate identity risk.
What Passkeys Get Right
Traditional authentication frequently relies on passwords combined with one-time passcodes, SMS messages, or push notifications. While stronger than passwords alone, these methods remain vulnerable to phishing, adversary-in-the-middle attacks, MFA fatigue, SIM swapping, and social engineering.
Passkeys fundamentally change that model. Instead of presenting a reusable secret, the user’s device holds a private cryptog…

But the $6.5 billion less that Microsoft spent than Wall Street forecast wasn't a sudden outbreak of unexpected restraint. It was delayed data centers that pushed some of its spending back.
Microsoft spent $45.2 billion on capital expenditures, including finance leases, in the September quarter, compared with the $51.7 billion expected by analysts cited by the Financial Times. That's still around 30% more than a year earlier, illustrating just how expensive the AI infrastructure race has become.
Redmond has now cut its calendar 2026 spending forecast from $175 billion to $170 billion, which is still an astronomical figure, admittedly.
CFO Amy Hood blamed delayed capacity deliveries from third parties, with those facilities now expected online in the second half of Microsoft's fiscal year. Spending will accelerate during that period, primarily because of all-too-familiar rising memory hardware costs.
Microsoft added 24 data centers during the quarter, but it also relies on smaller cloud operators. It's signed more than $80 billion in contracts with CoreWeave, Nebius and Nscale since 2023, according to the FT.
Some projects are struggling. Microsoft recently abandoned an Nscale capacity deal because of power constraints, while a Nebius facility in New Jersey is progressing more slowly than expected.

articles.title: AWS's Hydro team wants the compiler to catch coding agents' mistakes
articles.summary:
AWS’s Hydro team wants the compiler to catch coding agents’ mistakes
Earlier this month, the team behind Hydro developed a new way to check that a distributed system still works correctly when it resends messages after a failure.
This produced what Shadaj Laddad described to me as “like a 5000 line PR.” Hydro is an open-source Rust framework for distributed systems, the software that runs across many machines at once, and agents now write most of it with humans driving. The PR was difficult to split into smaller pieces as its components worked together.
That’s a lot of code to review for a tool developers count on to catch bugs. Laddad, research lead for the Hydro team at AWS, says it’s something the team spends a lot of time thinking about. I sat down with him last week at AGNTCon + MCPCon in San Jose. He was set to give a keynote the next day where he was going to argue code review can’t keep pace with how agents write code.
Agents have let the team aim higher, Laddad told me, saying PRs arrive faster and run longer. “You can have the feature work well in isolation, then you mix it with something else, and suddenly the guarantees break down,” he said.
And you can’t just trust the tests. In most agent workflows, he says, the agent writes both the code and the unit tests. “Agents are great, but they’re unpredictable,” Laddad said. articles.title: Auto-Generation Of Properties: Methodology Insertion
articles.summary:
Technology is only useful if it improves an existing methodology. Property generation is still refining that goal, but in the long term it could be very useful.
Key Takeaways:
A top-down semiconductor development flow has long been a goal for chip design, and shift left is certainly making that increasingly possible. The problem is that the starting point — the specification — is often incomplete or nonexistent, because the chip industry has been notoriously bad at writing specifications.
There are several ways to insert AI into existing flows. But just because something can be done doesn’t mean it should be. This is one of the big challenges facing AI adoption. Many existing tasks could be done more efficiently using an agentic flow, but it’s not clear whether that is the right thing to do.
This limitation becomes especially apparent when AI starts to help with something that has been woefully inadequate in the past — the creation of good, complete specifications. The big question is whether AI can enable designs, or verification environments, to be automatically derived from a specification. Perhaps a more correct goal is whether AI can help create better specifications. With better specifications, downstream design becomes a lot easier.

It also allows us to protect access to Reddit’s extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world.
Huffman also said that the login requirement will help Reddit better retain new users.

articles.title: CISA says max severity GitLab flaw now exploited in the wild
articles.summary:
Attackers have started exploiting a maximum-severity GitLab vulnerability patched earlier this month, according to the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA).
Tracked as CVE-2026-97229, this critical security flaw was discovered by a security researcher using the 'joaxcar' handle in the CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, which parses, compiles, and evaluates regular expressions in pipeline configuration files.
CVE-2026-97229 stems from an integer overflow weakness and could let remote attackers run arbitrary code on targeted instances via a maliciously crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient expression validation.
"GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation," it said.
GitLab addressed the security issue in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE) versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8 and urged admins to patch their servers immediately.
The company has also released threat detections to support customers with self-managed instances after detecting exploitation attempts.

The flat-fee pricing idea

The billing would have worked “like AWS,” he explained, where you “just do something and we send you a bill” rather than metering the exchange token by token. Altman does not name the model in question or give a timeline for when the change was under consideration.

The idea ran into resistance when OpenAI tried to gauge how customers felt about receiving a price with no breakdown. “The customer response on that is so negative,” Altman recounts, with buyers telling the company, “’I need to know what I’m paying for somehow.’”

Agentic AI has set off a firestorm in the world of CPUs over the past six months, yet it’s an area of performance that still doesn’t have solid, repeatable benchmarks to evaluate where the latest hardware falls. We’ve been working on an internal set of tests to evaluate at least one aspect of contentious agentic loops end-to-end, isolating CPU and memory performance from the accelerator to understand how these components contribute to the agentic loop.
This is still a work in progress, but we wanted to bring Tom’s Hardware Premium readers behind the scenes to understand how we’re going about tackling this problem, our methodology for testing, and detail what we’ve learned about agentic loops along the way. We've prototyped the test and settled the central design, but there's still work to do before the numbers it produces hold up to scrutiny.
Given that this area of computing is bleeding-edge and rapidly evolving, we undoubtedly have blind spots here. That’s OK. articles.title: SS7 and Diameter Attacks: How Signaling Flaws Expose Your Phone
articles.summary:
SS7 and Diameter signaling attacks can track, intercept, and impersonate you. Here’s how they work and how to stop them.
Your phone can be tracked, your SMS two-factor codes can be intercepted, and your number can be impersonated, all without malware, a phishing link, or any access to your device.
The attacks happen inside the telecom network, in the carrier-to-carrier control protocols known as signaling, the automated descendants of the old telephone switchboard. Most users never see them, and most carriers can’t reliably stop them.
Signaling attacks aren’t new. Most recently, they made headlines when Iranian-linked actors reportedly exploited outdated network technology to locate the phones of US personnel in the Middle East during the Iran war.
But the vulnerability has been around for decades, and it’s been used for far more everyday crimes, like intercepting bank one-time passcodes. It has even been demonstrated by popular YouTubers: Veritasium hijacked a tech influencer’s calls and texts using only his phone number.
This keeps happening
- Criminals have reportedly exploited signaling protocols in attacks on bank accounts and global telecom infrastructure.
- Citizen Lab exposed two long-running commercial surveillance campaigns abusing SS7 and Diameter, with thousands of attacks against targets in dozens of countries.

articles.title: Macbook Pro mit Touchscreen? Diese Apple-Gadgets hätte es unter Steve Jobs nicht gegeben
articles.summary:
Nicht nur das Macbook Pro mit Touchscreen: Diese Apple-Gadgets hätte es unter Steve Jobs nicht gegeben
Nach der Vorstellung des ersten Macbook Pro mit Touchscreen war Meme-Time in den sozialen Netzwerken. Viele Tech-Accounts posteten einen kurzen Ausschnitt von der Vorschau auf das Betriebssystem OS X Lion von 2010. Denn schon damals hatte der Apple-Mitgründer eine klare Meinung von Touch-Displays an Laptops.
Touchscreens wollen vertikal sein
    „Nach einem längeren Zeitraum wird Ihnen der Arm abfallen.“
Jobs war der Meinung, dass Touch-Oberflächen nicht vertikal sein wollen. Das funktioniere eben nicht, weil es ergonomisch furchtbar wäre. “Nach einer kurzen Zeit werden Sie ermüden und nach einem längeren Zeitraum wird Ihnen der Arm abfallen”, so Jobs. Stattdessen verwies er auf das damals schon existierende Multitouch-Trackpad, das ebenfalls Gesten wie „Pinch to Zoom“ unterstützt, mit dem Nutzer:innen Bilder vergrößern können. Das sei „der beste Weg, den wir gefunden haben, um ein Notebook um Multitouch zu erweitern“. Seine Aussagen untermauerte Jobs zudem mit Hinweis auf die Befragungen von Nutzer:innen.
Niemand will einen Stylus

articles.title: What five P99 CONF talks reveal about database trade-offs
articles.summary:
What five P99 CONF talks reveal about database trade-offs
P99 CONF is a virtual conference on high-performance, low-latency applications. Its 2026 event ran October 21–22. Here, we cover five of its 60-plus sessions. The recordings are available on demand at p99conf.io after registration.
Database storage design balances read amplification, write amplification, and space amplification (RUM conjecture). Improving one can increase another, depending on the workload and configuration. The five talks below show how engineers make those trade-offs across different database systems.
“Can Everything be an LSM?”
Almog Gavra, Co-Founder at Responsive (now Databricks)
Gavra frames database design around read amplification (data read per result), write amplification (data written per logical write), and space amplification (storage used relative to live data). A log favors fast writes but makes reads work harder; a sorted array does the reverse. As Gavra put it, “I think about LSM trees as a mechanism for tuning between these two extremes.”
LSMs were built for local disks, but their immutable files also fit object storage. Gavra points to Amazon S3’s lower storage cost, durability, and availability, then names the trade-offs: objects must be replaced rather than edited, each GET and PUT has a price, and cold reads are slower. articles.summary:
Tech whiz's internet-accessible Synology NAS gets bit by ransomware attack from 18-month-old remote code execution flaw — security updates neglected in a series of catastrophic errors
In their defense, Synology's misleading update policies didn't help.
Systems administrators are among the first to point out lax security policies in other companies' or people's setups. Sometimes, they are the ones who get bitten by not taking the same advice they will so readily dispense. Such is the tale of Reddit user NakamuraHwang, who had files on their Synology DS918+ NAS encrypted by a ransomware attack after making a series of unforced errors.
Hwang appears to be quite technically proficient and provided a detailed write-up of the situation. The key points, however, are that the unit in question (a) had its web interface exposed to the internet and (b) was roughly 18 months out-of-date with security patches. Just like the recent PHP snafu has adeptly shown, complacency is a far worse enemy than an army of AI bots.
The tech has a 3-2-1 backup setup, so they seemingly didn't lose any data. They attached the disks to a Proxmox machine for further inspection — Synology's DSM operating system uses mdraid underneath, so you can take the disks to another box and mount them there. Investigation of logs and the operating system files revealed that the attack was likely performed by abusing the CVE-2024-10441 remote code execution vulnerability, revealed a year and a half ago.

Mas isso só funciona quando os mesmos drivers podem ser instalados via Windows Update.
Na prática, o Cloud Rebuild permite fazer uma instalação nova e completa do Windows 11, evitando, por exemplo, que você se depare com um componente (como as saídas de áudio ou uma porta Ethernet) que não funciona após o procedimento ser realizado.

Gig workers are those who perform work or participate in a work arrangement and earn from such activities outside the traditional employer-employee relationship.
Platform workers are those who engage in work through or with online platforms.

Cette mention comptable, appelée « going concern » aux États-Unis, signifie que la direction n’est pas sûre de pouvoir financer l’entreprise d’ici un an. Dans la matinée, l’action du constructeur a perdu plus de 40 %, a relevé Electrek.
Pourtant, les ventes progressent : 241 motos électriques entre juillet et septembre 2026, contre 184 un an plus tôt. Sauf que la branche moto a perdu 17 millions de dollars d’exploitation sur la même période, soit environ 70 000 dollars (équivalent à 62 500 €) par moto vendue. Sa trésorerie est tombée de 82,8 millions de dollars fin 2025 à 39,9 millions au 30 septembre, et une dette arrive à échéance en décembre 2027.
Pour mémoire, Harley-Davidson avait sorti sa première moto électrique en 2019, avant de faire de LiveWire une marque à part entière en 2021. Depuis, la gamme s’est étoffée avec les modèles S2 Alpinista, Del Mar Mulholland et dernièrement avec les petites motos S4 Honcho. Aux États-Unis, LiveWire revendique 80 % des parts de marché sur les motos électriques de plus de 50 kW (67 ch) depuis janvier.

Cybercriminals are, once again, exploiting people’s interest in AI tools to distribute cryptojackers and make money - this time around, opting for a combination of spoofed popular products, trusty old GitHub, and a little SEO poisoning.

Nissan has a new version of its best-selling Rogue SUV, and it’s launching the model here with the latest version of its e-Power hybrid system, which Ars tested back in February. Most of the hybrid cars you can buy today are parallel hybrids, which means that they have an internal combustion engine and an electric motor, both of which drive some or all of the wheels—everything works in parallel. But there’s another approach. Instead of connecting the engine to the wheels via a transmission, it can act as a generator and charge the traction battery, which in turn powers the electric motor. Since the engine and motor work in series, this is known as a series hybrid.
That’s mostly how the Chevrolet Volt worked. As does Honda’s hybrid CR-V. Well, mostly; engineers worked out it was more efficient for those cars’ gasoline engines to directly drive the wheels at highway speeds, something that to this day makes a certain subset of hybrid car enthusiast irrationally angry. articles.title: Josep Albors, experto en ciberseguridad, sobre apagar el móvil como aconseja Sánchez: “Para la mayoría de los usuarios sirve de poco”
articles.summary:
Pedro Sánchez ha hablado de apagar el móvil 5 minutos cada día. Fue en La Revuelta donde lo comentaba en el momento en que hablaba sobre el tema del espionaje con Pegasus. Josep Albors, responsable de Investigación y Concienciación de ESET España, comenta: “Para la mayoría de los usuarios, que nos enfrentamos a amenazas más mundanas, este consejo, en materia de ciberseguridad, sirve de poco”. Además, dependiendo de cómo se instale y active, el programa malicioso tendrá efecto o no.
“Solo se aplica para casos concretos en los que el malware está presente en la memoria RAM, que se borra cuando reinicias el dispositivo”, explica Albors. El problema de esta memoria es que es temporal y se vacía al apagar el teléfono. En el caso de que la infección solo se active en memoria (sin persistencia), puede ser interrumpida por el apagado.
El problema es que, si el software malicioso está instalado en el terminal, al apagar y encender el móvil no va a desinstalar la app maligna. Así pues, puede volver a activarse al encenderlo. Además, no podemos estar seguros de que la infección haya desaparecido por el hecho de que el móvil vuelva a funcionar correctamente. Es necesario conocer la naturaleza de la amenaza y trabajar sobre su causa.

India's courts and sectoral regulators have already begun assigning liability for AI failures. Businesses that are holding out for a statute are preparing for the wrong deadline.
A bank has an AI system in place to flag suspicious transactions and take the call to freeze accounts. While the workflow has a human sign-off in place, clearing around 400 cases a day has resulted in the approval system becoming a formality. So, when a wrongly-frozen account takes the system to court, the bank becomes unable to prove what the human actually reviewed. This, unfortunately, is no longer a hypothetical scenario.
On July 2, 2026, the Supreme Court of India quashed orders passed by the National Company Law Tribunal and the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal in the Pooja Ramesh Singh v. Jammu and Kashmir Bank Ltd. case. The orders had rested on citations generated by an AI tool and attributed to the Supreme Court itself. This directed the Bar Council of India to constitute a committee to prescribe disciplinary norms for advocates who file AI-generated citations.
This is a business story as much as a legal one. Despite two tribunals and several rounds of proceedings, the parties had to carry the cost of a machine error that no human caught before filing. No AI statute was required to reach that outcome. Ordinary law, applied by judges, did the work.

articles.title: Le chiffrement qui protège les banques en ligne pourrait céder à un ordinateur quantique plus petit que prévu

Le chiffrement RSA-2048, qui protège la banque en ligne, les e-mails et les signatures numériques, pourrait lâcher prise face à un ordinateur quantique de seulement 23 000 qubits, contre près d'un million selon la dernière estimation de Google. C'est le record publié le jeudi 29 octobre par Alice & Bob, dans une prépublication déposée sur l'archive de l'IACR, l'association internationale de recherche en cryptologie. Avec la même recette, une clé Bitcoin tomberait en à peine une petite heure. Aucune machine de ce calibre n’existe encore, certes, mais le compte à rebours qui pèse sur la cryptographie d'Internet vient de prendre de la vitesse.
À peine 22 593 qubits pour faire tomber le chiffrement RSA
Imaginé en 1994 par le mathématicien américain Peter Shor, l'algorithme de Shor est une méthode de calcul conçue pour les ordinateurs quantiques, capable de décomposer un très grand nombre en facteurs premiers infiniment plus vite qu'une machine classique, ce qui en fait le cauchemar attitré des cryptographes. Or RSA protège une large part de notre Internet d'aujourd'hui, de la banque en ligne aux e-mails en passant par les signatures numériques. articles.title: Wie Solid-State-Transformatoren den Strombedarf von KI-Rechenzentren stemmen könnten
articles.summary:
Stromnetz am Limit: Wie Solid-State-Transformatoren jetzt Abhilfe schaffen könnten
Transformatoren sind ein zentraler, aber fast unsichtbarer Bestandteil unseres Stromnetzes: Die Großgeräte tragen dazu bei, Strom effizient über lange Entfernungen zu transportieren. Die Technik ist komplex und schwer zu bauen – immer noch. Da sich ihr grundlegendes Design seit etwa einem Jahrhundert kaum verändert hat, wären sie eigentlich reif für eine Modernisierung, doch die schien lange nicht zu passieren. Das ändert sich jetzt: Während die Welt darum kämpft, den steigenden Strombedarf von Elektrofahrzeugen, Rechenzentren und anderen Bereichen zu decken, suchen Forscher und Unternehmen nach Möglichkeiten, Transformatoren umzukrempeln. Und es gibt erste Erfolge: Neue Halbleiter-gestützte Varianten der Technik könnten dazu beitragen, Versorgungsengpässe teilweise zu lindern und sicherzustellen, dass das Stromnetz dem wachsenden Nachfragedruck standhalten kann.

articles.title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in record crypto heist
articles.summary:
Binance has suspended all withdrawals after the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange fell victim to what appears to be the biggest heist in history.
The exchange put the “estimated total impact” of the hack at about $6.3 billion and said around $3 billion of affected assets, mainly stablecoins that act as cash for the crypto market, had been frozen.
But analysts at Elliptic said the attacker had changed about $3.3 billion into digital assets that could not be frozen and was working to cash those out as traditional currency.
An “initial investigation” suggested hackers had been able to compromise an engineer’s laptop and withdraw funds from the platform, Binance said, adding on Friday morning that further investigation “has uncovered additional points of breach.” The company is working with law enforcement.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs linked the hack with a North Korean unit known as TraderTraitor, saying that the sums involved would make it “the largest crypto theft on record.” Last year, North Korean hackers stole crypto worth $1.5 billion in an attack on exchange Bybit.
Peter Ward, of the Sejong Institute in Seoul, said North Korea had considerable expertise and offered “near-total protection to its hackers.”
“Things may get a lot worse going forward,” he said.
Binance said on Friday that it had “already reserved over $6.34 billion of company funds to cover this incident,” with $5 billion of the funds “already held in the exact token assets that were impacted.”…

articles.title: GM to pay $220 million after selling customer Smart Driver data
articles.summary:
General Motors marketed its Smart Driver system as a way for parents to monitor teen drivers or for adults to track their driving behavior. But in 2024, it emerged that GM had been sharing that data with brokers. Those brokers then sold the data to insurance companies, and some drivers found that their insurance became more expensive as a result. To make matters worse, many of those drivers claimed they had no knowledge of ever agreeing to share such data for such purposes.
Last year, GM and its OnStar subsidiary entered into a settlement with the FTC, prohibiting them from sharing some kinds of driver data with third parties. The settlement was finalized this January. That agreement banned the two companies from sharing geolocation data or driver behavior data for five years. At the time, GM also discontinued Smart Driver across its entire range.
Now the automaker has reached terms with the District of Columbia and 35 states after their attorneys general joined together to sue GM as well.
GM told Reuters in a statement that “[s]afer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to being clear about what information is used, how it’s protected, and the choices customers have about what they share.”
According to TechCrunch, the settlement with the states is notable in that it doesn’t take GM’s word that it’s complying with the privacy policy—a third party will be required to make that determination.

Le phénomène existe bien, mais ses effets sur la météo en France dans les prochaines semaines restent très incertains, y compris pour les prévisionnistes.
Selon La Chaîne Météo, dans un tweet diffusé ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, « le vortex polaire pourrait se faire bousculer par un réchauffement stratosphérique (SSW) très précoce début novembre », plus exactement aux alentours du 6 novembre. La chaîne d’information météorologique estime que « ce SSW serait un record de précocité », mais juge ses conséquences en France encore très incertaines.
Qu’est-ce que le vortex polaire ?
Comme l’explique Météo-France, le vortex polaire correspond à une « zone de basses pressions en altitude centrée sur les pôles géographiques ». Cette zone est toujours présente près des pôles, indique le National Weather Service, qui précise bien qu’il ne s’agit pas d’un phénomène nouveau. « Le terme ‘vortex polaire’ n’a été popularisé que récemment, attirant ainsi l’attention sur un phénomène météorologique qui a toujours existé », souligne le service météorologique des États-Unis.
Ce vortex peut influencer la météo, y compris en France, en fonction de sa position ou de son réchauffement, en engendrant potentiellement une vague de froid.

Doomformer: Diese KI wurde in Doom geschaffen – was sie leisten kann
Egal, ob in der Google-Suche oder auf einem Satelliten der ESA: Doom wurde mittlerweile auf so vielen verschiedenen Plattformen spielbar gemacht, dass die meisten Gamer:innen wohl schon lange mit dem Zählen aufgehört haben. Etwas seltener sind die Versuche, etwas anderes als einen Ego-Shooter aus Doom zu machen. So versucht es derzeit der Entwickler, der sich auf GitHub den Nicknamen „mottopanikeiku“ gegeben hat.
Doom als KI? Wie das funktionieren soll
Sein Projekt trägt den Namen „Doomformer“ und ist eine Wortneuschöpfung aus Doom und einem Transformermodell. Im Grunde hat er den Ego-Shooter in ein neuronales Netzwerk umgewandelt, das in der Lage ist, Arithmetik durchzuführen. Um das zu realisieren, nutzt er sogenannte „Voodoo Dolls“ aus Doom. Das sind Klone der Spielfigur, die immer dann auftauchen, wenn das Spiel einen zusätzlichen Spielerstartpunkt im Level entdeckt.
Um das neuronale Netzwerk zu bauen, werden laut dem Entwickler 1.355 Voodoo-Puppen genutzt, die zusammen ein MNIST-Netzwerk auf der Map bilden. Die Puppen fahren auf Bahnen hin und her und überqueren dabei Linien, die als Gewichtungen fungieren. Kommt es zu einer Aktivierung der Puppen, wird eine bestimmte Anzahl über eine Treppe nach oben in die zweite Ebene befördert. Das passiert, weil das Überqueren jeder Linie das Licht und die Ebenenhöhe verändern kann. So können sie Elemente im Spiel verändern und etwa Zahlen anzeigen.

articles.title: Ukraine uses new unspooling ground drones for dangerous frontline wire work
articles.summary:
Ukraine is getting ground robots to carry out one of the riskiest battlefield tasks — and they're doing an excellent job
Ukraine deploys custom wheeled UGVs for dangerous frontline missions
- A wheeled robot lays battlefield wire while engineers remain under cover
- A remote-controlled frame unwinds wire across exposed battlefield terrain without nearby engineers
- Ukrainian ground-robot missions rose from 7,511 in January to 19,940 in July 2026
Ukrainian troops are using remotely-operated wheeled robots to construct defensive obstacles in dangerous locations where military engineers face direct exposure.
The ground robot carries coils of wire on specially designed frames, releasing the material across designated areas as it moves forward.
Images from the Ukrainian military show one of these autonomous vehicles with six wheels, but the manufacturer and model remain unknown.
Ground robots take over dangerous engineering duties
The ground robot comes with a specially constructed framework mounted above its wheels that helps it to hold the wire rolls in place.
Its sloping support structure permits the material to unwind gradually while the machine advances, creating obstacles along the chosen route.
This machine is remotely operated by Ukraine's 16th Separate Support Brigade while remaining under cover.
This minimizes the risk and removes the need for engineering teams to stand outside protected positions while manually deploying wire across exposed terrain.

articles.title: Rogers expands satellite-to-mobile coverage internationally
articles.summary:
Rogers has announced that it is taking its satellite-to-mobile coverage internationally, bringing the service to Japan, Australia, and New Zealand.
“Canadians want to stay connected wherever their travels take them,” writes Mark Kennedy, Rogers’ Chief Technology Officer. “With satellite-to-mobile roaming in Japan, Australia, and New Zealand, we’re extending coverage to more destinations around the world so customers can stay connected when travelling abroad.”
Rogers notes that the launch expands its international satellite-to-mobile roaming footprint to four countries, after expanding service to the US earlier this year.
Rogers also uses Elon Musk’s Starlink to operate its satellite-to-mobile service. Using Starlink, customers can access apps like WhatsApp, Messenger, and X (god forbid you need to send a tweet in the middle of nowhere), along with Google Maps, AllTrails, and weather updates from AccuWeather.
The telecom giant notes in the press release that international satellite-to-mobile roaming is included in the $100/mo Ultimate plans, alongside eligible Roam Like Home options and select Travel Passes (International and International + Cruises).

articles.title: North Korean hackers blamed for stealing record $6.3B in Binance breach | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Hackers working for the North Korean regime have been blamed for a record cryptocurrency heist following a cyberattack at crypto exchange Binance. The hackers stole at least $6.3 billion in crypto from the company’s wallets, though about half of that amount was frozen as the stolen crypto traveled across various blockchains, according to security researchers.
The breach is by far the largest known theft of crypto in history, though the incident has not been confirmed yet to be resolved, and the amount of crypto stolen may change.
In a post on X, Binance said its initial investigation showed that the hackers broke into the company’s network after targeting a “compromised” Binance engineer’s laptop, which “allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.”
Binance said it has seen no evidence of a leak of its private keys, which would grant the hacker near-unfettered control over the company’s stores of crypto.
The crypto exchange — the world’s largest — said it has now suspended all deposits and withdrawals while its investigation into the breach continues. TechCrunch reported on Thursday that the exchange had paused withdrawals across some of its blockchains.
Binance said “user funds are safe,” but did not immediately provide proof of this claim. The company said it will “publish an updated proof of reserves once the remediation is complete.”

articles.title: Cuando pienses que la cera de tus oídos es molesta y asquerosa, piensa que sería peor tener insectos ahí dentro
articles.summary:
El cerumen que se acumula en nuestros oídos para muchas personas es asqueroso e innecesario, puesto que puede generar tapones que nos generan una disminución en la capacidad de escucha. Pero aunque para un buen grupo de la población la cera de los oídos es sinónimo de una falta de higiene, para la biología es un sofisticado sistema de seguridad biomecánico que evita que los insectos colonicen nuestro oído.
Dos propiedades. Tras estudiar el cerumen de nuestros oídos, los investigadores han entendido la compleja mecánica que hay detrás, puesto que se ha visto que tiene dos propiedades que aparentemente son contradictorias: es resbaladizo y pegajoso al mismo tiempo.
Una trampa mortal. Para entender cómo el cerumen frena a los intrusos, los investigadores recurrieron a la biomimética y a pruebas de comportamiento con hormigas. Y es que debemos tener en cuenta que los insectos son escaladores excepcionales gracias a que segregan unas gotas adhesivas en sus patas, lo que les permite desafiar la gravedad y caminar por techos o paredes verticales.
Pero el canal auditivo es un terreno hostil, ya que el cerumen es una sustancia hidrófila, porosa y viscoelástica. De esta manera, cuando un insecto intenta caminar sobre una capa de cerumen liso, se cae inmediatamente, puesto que los microporos de la cera absorben los fluidos adhesivos que segrega el propio insecto, anulando su capacidad de agarre.

articles.title: Anatomy of a Business Email Scam: How Fake Invoices Slip Past Busy Bookkeepers - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Understanding the Rising Threat of Business Email Scams
In today’s fast-paced business environment, email remains a primary communication tool, especially for financial transactions like invoicing and payments. However, this reliance has made businesses, particularly their finance teams and bookkeepers, prime targets for increasingly sophisticated email scams. One of the most prevalent tactics involves fake invoice scams, where cybercriminals impersonate legitimate vendors or partners to trick businesses into paying fraudulent invoices.
The scale of this threat is staggering. With 94% of malware delivered via email and phishing attacks accounting for over 90% of data breaches, email-based scams have become the favored method for cybercriminals aiming to exploit businesses. According to the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center, business email compromise (BEC) scams led to losses exceeding $2.4 billion in 2023 alone. These numbers reflect not only the monetary damage but also the operational disruptions and reputational harm businesses face.
As these scams evolve, understanding their anatomy is critical to strengthening defenses. This article delves into how fake invoices slip past busy bookkeepers, what makes these scams so effective, and crucially, how businesses can protect themselves.

At TechSparks 2026, Tagbin Co-founders Saurav Bhaik and Ankit Sinha demonstrated how BRIXX uses natural-language prompts to bring architectural design, construction planning, and cost estimation together on a single platform.

articles.title: AI firms want to build underwater data centers in the middle of an endangered whale habitat — but Alaskan campaigners have branded the plans 'really outrageous'
articles.summary:
'We're deeply concerned': Underwater AI data centers proposed for Maine and Alaska — but critics say they could endanger whale species
The latest AI data center controversy is under the waves
- AI firm DeepGreen has suggested building data centers underwater
- This would help to keep the locations cool and running efficiently
- But the proposed locations could seriously harm endangered whale species
AI data centers need an awful lot of water to keep their machines running at optimal temperatures, and that creates a problem: just how do you get that much water on-site? One potential solution seems almost blindingly obvious: why not build them underwater? Yet as residents across the US are discovering, that idea is proving to be highly controversial.
Take the recently-pitched $100m underwater data center located off the coasts of Maine and Alaska, for example. AI firm DeepGreen Holdings has proposed building data centers off Western Passage, Maine, and Upper Cook Inlet, Alaska, and they would cover some 1,650 acres and comprise 66 compute pods and 300 tidal turbines.
The problem? Both locations are home to endangered whale populations that could be significantly impacted by the developments. In the case of the Maine site, the Gulf of Maine is linked to critical habits for the North Atlantic right whale. As for Upper Cook Inlet, that’s a designated critical habitat for the endangered Cook Inlet beluga whale.

Auf der Store-Seite versprach der PDF-Reader, eine Office-App zu sein, mit der User:innen „PDF-Dateien öffnen können, die lokal auf ihrem Smartphone gespeichert sind.“ Dabei würde die App sogar PDFs unterstützen, die mit einem Passwort geschützt wurden. articles.title: 267 ventes par mois : le nouveau SUV électrique chinois de Volkswagen vire au fiasco total
articles.summary:
Pour tenir le rythme, Volkswagen développe continuellement une gamme dédiée au marché chinois. Mieux encore, la marque allemande s’est carrément alliée à Xpeng pour cerner au mieux les attentes locales. Elle pensait alors avoir trouvé la recette magique pour renouer avec le succès. Hélas, la mayonnaise a bien du mal à prendre puisque le premier modèle de cette collaboration s’avère être un échec.
Les chiffres de ThinkerCar sont sans appel : avec 267 exemplaires vendus chaque mois, l’ID. Unyx 08 est complètement à la traîne. Par rapport aux objectifs de Volkswagen qui étaient fixés à 3 622 modèles par mois, c’est la douche froide. Le constructeur allemand, qui a vu ses ventes fortement chuter en Chine, comptait pourtant beaucoup sur cette nouvelle génération de modèles pour remonter la pente.
L’alliance avec Xpeng : l’espoir déchu de Volkswagen
Cela semble malgré tout très insuffisant pour contrer la concurrence locale qui bataille à feu et à sang à coup de prix ultra agressifs. articles.title: Smarter Power Sequencing with GreenPAK™ - EE Times
articles.summary:
Programmable mixed-signal devices can replace sprawling RC networks and firmware-dependent control with compact, deterministic, and adaptable multi-rail sequencing.
Modern processors, FPGAs, memory modules, sensors, and high-speed interfaces rarely operate from a single supply. Each device may require several voltage rails, and those rails often must rise and fall in a defined order. A core supply may need to stabilize before an I/O rail; a memory rail may need to follow a processor rail; and a reset signal may not be released until every relevant voltage is valid. If that choreography is wrong, the result can be excessive inrush current, back-powering, latch-up, corrupted initialization, or, in some cases, device damage.
Why traditional sequencing becomes difficult
The simplest sequencer uses RC delays and logic gates to shift regulator-enable signals. That approach can be adequate for a small, fixed design, but it becomes unwieldy as rail count and supervision requirements grow. Every added stage introduces more passives, more tolerance stack-up, and more potential failure points. Capacitor and resistor variation, temperature, leakage, and aging can shift the effective delay. A timing change late in development may require component substitutions, schematic edits, new layout work, and another board spin.
A microcontroller offers more flexibility, but it also introduces software into a function that may be required before the main processor is ready. Firmware has to boot, ex…

articles.title: Underwater data centers are heading for waters that endangered whales call home

In context: Pilot projects have demonstrated that undersea data centers can operate reliably without significant heat-dissipation issues. However, underwater environments support fragile ecosystems that could be seriously disrupted by artificial computing infrastructure.
Earlier this year, DeepGreen Holdings filed a preliminary permit application with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC). The company is seeking to develop two data center projects designed to take advantage of underwater environments, but the proposed locations overlap with habitats of two endangered whale populations. Local communities have also voiced strong opposition to the projects.
DeepGreen plans to build its facilities beneath Cook Inlet, in Alaska, and in the Gulf of Maine. The proposed Cook Inlet facility would consist of 66 modular data center "pods," powered by 330 to 350 tidal turbines. The company expects the installation to generate 100 megawatts of power, most of which would be used to run the underwater data center.
The Maine project would be smaller, with 50 tidal turbines providing 51 megawatts of power to a cluster of data center pods. Both projects could affect the habitats of two distinct endangered whale populations. Cook Inlet is home to a genetically isolated population of beluga whales, while the Gulf of Maine serves as a feeding ground for North Atlantic right whales.

In a nutshell: Data centers have already drawn widespread resistance over their impact on electricity prices and water supplies, and estimates of how their energy use might affect carbon emissions have recently grown. Still, projections vary widely, owing to uncertainty over renewables and over how many data centers will actually be built in the next several years.
In a report obtained by Bloomberg, the environmental nonprofit Sierra Club estimates that planned US AI data centers would add 618 million metric tons to the power sector's carbon emissions between 2025 and 2030, a 42% increase. The figure would effectively reverse 15 years of greenhouse gas reductions from electricity generation.
Adding that much CO2 would bring the sector's 2030 emissions to 2.1 billion metric tons. The latest estimate of the AI buildout's effect is between two and four times what the group would have projected a year and a half ago.
Many of these data centers are turning to new power sources of their own to avoid waiting to plug into existing grids. While that might ease the strain on residential grids and electricity prices, these off-grid sources could add more than 460 million metric tons of emissions, roughly equal to Mexico's annual emissions.

A companhia não está abandonando a IA. A mudança é de foco: em vez de premiar quem usa mais ferramentas ou gera mais código, a Amazon quer avaliar o impacto do trabalho sobre clientes, negócios e equipes.
Um dos problemas é o chamado “tokenmaxxing”, expressão usada para descrever o consumo exagerado de tokens para elevar indicadores internos. Tokens são as unidades usadas pelos modelos para processar e gerar informações e também influenciam o custo de operação dessas ferramentas.
Segundo a Fortune, a Amazon alerta que transformar esse consumo em objetivo pode aumentar despesas sem necessariamente melhorar os resultados. O problema não é apenas teórico. Funcionários da companhia chegaram a executar agentes de IA em tarefas desnecessárias só para elevar seus números em um ranking interno descontinuado em maio.
Para o vice-presidente da Amazon, Terk Terkowitz, o melhor critério são os resultados obtidos no longo prazo. Isso inclui impacto para clientes, para o negócio e para as próprias equipes. Indicadores como consumo de tokens e adoç…

Eso borraría 15 años de reducciones, según un análisis interno del Sierra Club, organización ambientalista estadounidense.

The Verge añadió que ese aumento equivale a la electricidad que consumen más de 128 millones de hogares en un año.
La mayor parte del incremento no pasaría por la red convencional. Más de 460 millones de toneladas vendrían de plantas que las tecnológicas construyen por su cuenta, fuera de la red, para no esperar la conexión. Jeremy Fisher, asesor principal de clima y energía del Sierra Club, dijo que esa cifra equivale a las emisiones anuales de México.
Las centrales conectadas a la red sumarían otras 154 millones de toneladas, un aumento de 10% sobre la proyección base de 2030. Un análisis aparte de las organizaciones Earthjustice y Better Data Center Project estima que hasta cuatro quintas partes de la energía de los proyectos autónomos podrían salir del gas natural.

articles.title: Algo extremadamente raro está pasando en el ártico: la rotura del vértice polar más temprana desde que tenemos registros
articles.summary:
El lunes 26 de octubre, con los datos de las 12 de la noche, 18 de los 50 escenarios que calcula cada día el Centro Europeo de Predicción a Medio Plazo decían que el vórtice polar iba a romperse en los quince días siguientes. Doce horas después eran 23. El martes, 43. El jueves 29, los 50 decían eso mismo.
No es solo algo de Europa. En los últimos tres o cuatro días, los principales modelos de predicción han ido confluyendo en la misma idea: que el vórtice va a sufrir una inversión (con los vientos de la estratosfera cambiando de sentido) entre el 4 y el 10 de noviembre.
Si ocurre, tendremos entre manos un calentamiento súbito estratosférico, sí; pero no uno cualquiera. El más temprano desde 1958: unas tres semanas antes del que hasta ahora tenía el récord. Esto lo podemos dar casi por hecho. Lo que pase luego, nadie lo sabe.
¿Qué es exactamente el vórtice polar? Se trata de una corriente de fuertes vientos (oeste → este) que gira en torno a las grandes reservas de aire frío que se encuentran sobre los polos del planeta. Se forma en la estratosfera; es decir, a unos 16–48 kilómetros de altura. En sentido metafórico (o 'periodístico' si me apuran), el vórtice polar es lo que encierra el frío en el polo.
La lógica nos dice que, en verano, el vórtice se reduce hasta la mínima expresión y, aunque es cierto que nunca lo hemos visto desaparecer del todo en estas fechas, se hace tan débil que apenas influye en el tiempo del hemisferio.

Le processeur ne fait pas tout. Pour vendre un ordinateur, il faut aussi pouvoir l’équiper en mémoire à un prix acceptable. C’est précisément là que le marché se grippe : les composants deviennent plus chers, les machines aussi, et les acheteurs se montrent moins pressés de renouveler leur équipement. Face à des ventes moins dynamiques, les constructeurs cherchent à écouler les ordinateurs qu’ils ont déjà en stock et réduisent leurs commandes. Pour Intel, la conséquence est immédiate : moins de machines à assembler signifie aussi moins de processeurs à vendre. Le groupe anticipe un recul du marché du PC d’environ 12 % en 2026, puis de 10 % supplémentaires en 2027.

articles.title: DirectX Raytracing Gets Clustered Geometry for Higher FPS and Up to 90% VRAM Savings
articles.summary:
Thursday, October 29th 2026
DirectX Raytracing Gets Clustered Geometry for Higher FPS and Up to 90% VRAM Savings
Microsoft has released one of the most significant updates to its DirectX Raytracing (DXR) since its debut in 2018. This update officially introduces clustered geometry and partitioned top-level acceleration structure (PTLAS). With clustered geometry, Microsoft envisions scenes where all animated and generated geometry is broken down into simple, reusable clusters of triangles. Typically, scenes repeatedly build large bottom-level acceleration structures, which incur additional compute costs. By using clustered geometry, ray tracing can utilize full detailed geometry used for standard rasterization instead of proxies, ensuring that ray-traced shadows and reflections match the currently visible scene.
In open-world games, using a top-level acceleration structure (TLAS) can lead to massive VRAM and compute demands. To address this, DXR now introduces partitioned TLAS (PTLAS), allowing ray tracing to focus on changes in a specific region while retaining acceleration-structure data elsewhere. Clustered geometry and PTLAS can be used together or separately, with no limitations. Below image is NVIDIA's sample of clustered geometry in action, visualized in three stages: default, clusters, and triangles applied.Benchmarks follow.

Des hackers cherchent à s’engouffrer dans une brèche qui peut exposer un site WordPress pendant sa mise à jour. La version 7.1.4 corrige le problème depuis le 28 octobre, mais Wordfence a déjà repéré plus de 18 500 requêtes suspectes.
Il n’a fallu que quelques heures pour que des attaquants tentent de profiter de l’une des failles corrigées par WordPress 7.1.4. Le 28 octobre dernier, Wordfence, le spécialiste de la sécurité des sites WordPress, a ainsi repéré une première requête suspecte neuf minutes seulement après l’activation de sa règle de protection, elle-même déployée environ trois heures après la publication de la mise à jour.
Le piège se cache dans les fichiers temporaires
La faille, signalée par le chercheur Umut Bayram, concerne le cœur de WordPress, des versions 4.7 à 7.1.3. Lors de certaines mises à jour utilisant un paquet complet du logiciel, les fichiers sont décompressés dans un dossier temporaire au nom prévisible, sous wp-content/upgrade. Cette copie contient un installateur auquel un visiteur peut accéder si le serveur laisse ce répertoire accessible et autorise l’exécution de PHP. Dans ces conditions, un attaquant sans compte peut parvenir à exécuter du code sur le serveur.
Les hackers doivent toutefois accéder à l’installateur temporaire avant que WordPress ne supprime les fichiers. Selon les essais rapportés par Wordfence, ils ne disposent que de quelques secondes. Ils envoient donc des requêtes à répétition dans l’espoir de surprendre un site au moment…

Depuis le début du mois, Apple et Microsoft figurent dans le registre russe des « organisateurs de diffusion d'information ». Concrètement, les deux groupes doivent garder les échanges de leurs utilisateurs en Russie et les remettre aux services de sécurité sur demande.
Ce registre est géré par Roskomnadzor, le régulateur russe des télécoms, lequel y avait déjà ajouté Google Meet en janvier.
Messages, appels, métadonnées : ce que Moscou peut réclamer
Puisque les deux géants sont désormais dans le registre, ils doivent non seulement stocker les messages, les appels audio et les vidéos des utilisateurs russes, mais aussi les fournir aux agences de sécurité dès qu’elles le demandent. Notons que le processus est effectué sans procédure judiciaire. D’après Bloomberg, elles doivent aussi garder pendant trois ans les informations sur les utilisateurs et sur la transmission de leurs échanges. Cela correspond aux métadonnées, c’est-à-dire aux interlocuteurs et à l’horaire plutôt qu’au contenu. Le tout doit rester sur des serveurs situés en Russie, donc soumis au droit russe.
Apple et Microsoft rejoignent Google Meet, WhatsApp, Telegram, Snapchat, Cloudflare ou encore Blizzard Entertainment. Les entreprises qui refusent s’exposent à des amendes, puis à une restriction d’accès à leur service dans le pays. Ni Apple ni Microsoft n’ont commenté, ni indiqué si elles comptaient se conformer à ces règles.

Between the executive briefings and keynotes, theoretical physicist, City College of New York professor, and best-selling author Michio Kaku gave a talk on the waves of innovation (Figure 1). The idea is closely associated with economist Joseph Schumpeter, whose theory of creative destruction states that new inventions render older ones obsolete.
Kaku traced these waves from steam power during the Industrial Revolution, through the transistor and the Information Age, to today’s AI revolution. He then looked ahead to how quantum computing, brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), and other advances could give rise to entirely new industries and transform life as we know it. As with many of Kaku’s talks, it was a thought-provoking glimpse into what the future could hold at our current pace of technological advancement.
Semiconductors at the center

articles.title: Smaller Components Complicate BGA Rework Heating- EE Times
articles.summary:
Smaller components and denser boards are creating new thermal challenges for ball grid array (BGA) rework. Miniature passives can be located within a millimeter or two of rework targets. This tightens thermal profile windows and raises the stakes for precision heat delivery. Traditional hot-air systems that operated at larger scales struggle to meet the demands of today’s high-density assemblies.
The SMT miniaturization trend behind modern PCB design
The drive toward higher functionality in smaller form factors has pushed surface mount technology (SMT) miniaturization to the forefront of PCB design priorities. Designers are packing more components into less space, with passive components such as 0201 and 01005 footprints increasingly used in high-density applications.
The International Electronics Manufacturing Initiative (iNEMI) electronics roadmap identifies component miniaturization and increased packing density as important industry drivers, with HDI microvia sizes continuing to shrink as manufacturers push toward finer geometries. This trend creates new challenges for rework operations that were engineered around larger geometries.
Proximity and warpage risks in high-density assemblies
As spacing tightens, the gap between a target BGA and its neighboring 0201 or 01005 passives can fall below a millimeter. Standard hot-air nozzles weren’t designed for this proximity.

The race to deploy AI agents finds a familiar hurdle in data access
Enterprises racing to put AI agents into production are discovering that role-based access control, not model choice, decides whether those agents can be trusted. Rising inference costs, privacy worries and sovereignty demands are also pulling more AI workloads back inside corporate data centers.
That shift favors companies that have spent years governing sensitive data at scale. Cloudera Inc. is betting on Cloudera Anywhere Cloud, a hybrid data and AI platform that spans public clouds and on-premises environments. The company has long been strong on governance, security and scalability but weaker on usability, a gap the new platform was built to close, according to Leo Brunnick (pictured), chief product officer of Cloudera.
“It turns out that the model is ultimately not going to be what separates your success from your competitor’s success,” Brunnick said. “The things that are going to separate you are, number one, your unique data. Your unique data and your unique processes, your alpha — what makes you a business.”
Brunnick spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight and Paul Gillin at EVOLVE26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. articles.title: « Le SMS de la mort » : ce simple message peut rendre votre smartphone inutilisable
articles.summary:
Le chercheur indépendant en cybersécurité Mark Blaszczyk a rendu publique une faille zero day sur Android. Pas de panique, elle a été corrigée par Google avant et votre téléphone ne court aucun risque. Mais le fonctionnement de cette faille est tout à fait intéressant.
Un « SMS of Death » qui peut faire des dégâts sur votre smartphone Android
Mark Blaszczyk a donc publié le résultat de ses recherches sur Internet et il décrit en détail comment fonctionne cette faille. Elle se trouve dans le composant Android plus très utilisé, un ancien format de « data SMS », utilisé historiquement pour des notifications de MMS ou des contenus push. Il n’apparaît jamais à l’écran, puisqu’il se contente de fonctionner en arrière-plan. Le problème vient en réalité d’une conversion mal encadrée : Android lit la longueur de l’en-tête d’un message comme un entier long, puis la convertit en entier signé 32 bits sans vérifier que la valeur reste plausible.
Avec la séquence de cinq octets 88 80 80 80 00, cette valeur devient -2147483648. Face à ça, Android tente alors de créer un tableau d’octets de cette taille négative, ce qui tue le processus com.android.phone qui gère… la téléphonie, rien que ça. Chaque message malformé comme cela coupe donc le service durant une à deux secondes, le temps que ce processus redémarre. Ce qui coupe tout simplement les appels en cours.
Une faille bien particulière, puisqu’elle est qualifiée de zero click, c’est-à-dire que la victime n’a rien à ouvrir, installer ou v…

Thursday, October 29th 2026
PSA: Fake KytyPS5 and AnyPS5 Repos on GitHub Are Spreading Malware
Fake GitHub repositories posing as two PS5 projects, the KytyPS5 emulator and the AnyPS5 porting tool, are being used to spread password-stealing malware, according to NordVPN's Threat Intelligence team. As reported by Tom's Hardware, visitors get pointed to a ZIP file whose Windows executable unpacks a hidden multi-stage loader. The loader first checks whether it's on a real gaming PC, and exits if the system has less than 2 GB of RAM or no physical GPU, or looks like a virtual machine or cloud server. It seems built to dodge sandboxes and security researchers. Here's how NordVPN CTO Marijus Briedis put it:
Emulation fans are a perfect target. They are used to downloading experimental software from GitHub and running unsigned files, so nothing about this feels suspicious. But this is not an emulator. It steals your data, hides from your antivirus and erases its own tracks before you notice anything is wrong.
On a machine that passes the aforementioned checks, the malware adds Microsoft Defender exclusion rules, then decrypts and runs a packed payload that NordVPN believes is an infostealer. A cleanup script wipes the files about two minutes later. Its self-signed certificates carry fake company names and were created the same day the malware was built, so the campaign may be automated.

articles.title: Hackers Exploited Cisco SD-WAN Flaw to Plant Malware Built to Steal Encryption Keys
articles.summary:
Hackers exploited a critical Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN flaw, fixed in February, to plant custom malware inside the systems that control an organization's SD-WAN network.
The malware, called KeyDrift, is designed to copy the keys that encrypt traffic between sites and store them for later use, Cisco Talos said on October 28. Talos calls the attacks historical but does not specify when they occurred or whether any keys were sent.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-20127 and has a CVSS score of 10.0. It allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authentication and gain administrative privileges on these control systems. On a Controller, the attacker can log in as a high-privileged internal account that is not root.
When Cisco disclosed the flaw in February, Talos tracked its exploitation as UAT-8616, a cluster of activity it said went back to at least 2023.
In Cisco's traditional key exchange, each SD-WAN router periodically generates an AES key for its traffic and sends it to the Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart). The Controller passes the keys on to other routers. A process on the Controller called vdaemon runs the encrypted control connections that carry these keys.
On a compromised Controller, a KeyDrift component called LittleFilch hooks into vdaemon and reads control messages after they are decrypted. For a preset list of edge routers, it pulls out their IP addresses and a 32-byte field. Talos assesses that field as the AES-256 key material that the Controller…

An attacker tried to exploit a critical GitLab vulnerability on the Alpine Linux project's own GitLab server a week after GitLab released a fix, Alpine Linux said on 28 October.
The flaw, CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS score: 10.0), can let an attacker run code on a GitLab server through a crafted regular expression in a CI configuration. Alpine found no evidence that the attack worked but cannot rule it out, so it rebuilt the server from scratch and reset every account's password.
GitLab's fix is a set of patches to the Ruby that GitLab ships in its own packages and container images. Alpine's GitLab image used standard Ruby, so upgrading the server to GitLab 19.3.6 on 22 October did not fix the flaw.
For anyone running GitLab on their own Ruby, built from source or in their own container image, "upgrading GitLab is not enough," Alpine said. Those servers also need Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12, 4.0.9 or later, and users of Alpine's alpinelinux/gitlab image need to pull 19.3.6 again.
The server gitlab.alpinelinux.org hosts aports, the repository from which Alpine's packages are built. Packages built from 20 to 24 October, and the 21 October releases, came from aports changes verified against records outside GitLab, according to Alpine.
Those releases include the minirootfs files that the official Alpine Docker images are built from. Alpine is extending the checks to 27 October, when it closed the server. The keys that sign its packages and releases have never been on the GitLab server.

articles.title: GitHub Launches npm Firewall to Block Malicious Packages Before Installation
articles.summary:
GitHub has announced that it's introducing a new package firewall as a preview to block installation of suspicious npm packages during installation time.
"The firewall inspects both metadata requests and package downloads for signs of malicious activity, acting as an install-time policy gate," GitHub said.
The feature, which currently supports only npm packages, is available in public preview for all GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers, including data-resident GitHub Enterprise Cloud.
According to the Microsoft subsidiary, the firewall is placed between endpoints or internal registries and the upstream package repositories so as to deter malware attacks that compromise systems when packages are installed.
This behavior can expose users to severe security risks, especially when artificial intelligence (AI) agents and CI runners automatically install dependencies to complete a task or build without their explicit permission.

articles.title: 26,400 Valid Cloud and AI Credentials Found Exposed in Public Gitee Repositories
articles.summary:
26,400 credentials that developers left in public code on Gitee, a Chinese code-hosting service, still worked when a researcher tested them. Anyone who copied one from that code could have used it.
Independent researcher Ben Zimmermann found them by scanning 7.25 million public Gitee repositories and reported the results on October 28. Most were keys for cloud and AI services, led by 9,473 Alibaba Cloud AccessKey pairs.
Zimmermann sent the vendors with the most exposed keys a list of their credentials, but he did not contact the developers who leaked them. When he published, he had not confirmed that any of the reported credentials had been revoked. So anyone who has pushed a key to a public Gitee repository cannot assume it has been revoked.
The scan ran for about a month, but Zimmermann did not provide the dates, so it is unclear how long ago the credentials were tested. He also did not say whether anyone else had used them.
He ran two secret scanners, TruffleHog and Kingfisher, over every repository. Both tried each credential against the service that issued it and kept only those that worked, he wrote.
The scanners read each repository's full commit history. A key that a developer later removed from the code could still be found and counted there.
The 26,400 figure counts each credential once, regardless of how many repositories it appeared in. By commit date, 12,242 of the credentials came from 2025, nearly half the total. Some dated to the late 2000s.

articles.title: Telegram Android Flaw Lets Attackers Run Code When Users Answer Voice Calls
articles.summary:
A flaw in Telegram for Android could be chained with two other bugs to take full control of a victim's phone through a voice call, once the victim answered, according to security startup NebuSec.
The attacker needed only an ordinary Telegram account. Telegram fixed the flaw in version 12.10.4 of the app, released in late September, and NebuSec disclosed it on October 29.
Combined with an information-leak bug, the flaw gives the attacker an escape from the Telegram app to Android, NebuSec co-founder and chief executive Eten Zou told The Hacker News. Adding an Android root exploit then gives full control of the phone, including its messages, microphone and camera.
The flaw can be triggered in every version from 8.6.2 through 12.10.3, Zou said. Those versions came out between March 2022 and September 2026.
The company confirmed it in private voice calls on ARM64-based phones and has no evidence so far that it directly affects Telegram's iOS and desktop apps or group calls.
Anyone using Telegram for Android should make sure the app is on version 12.10.4 or later. The version number appears at the bottom of the app's Settings page. The flaw had no CVE identifier as of October 29.
The attack needs the victim to be called and to answer, Zou said, so setting Telegram's call privacy option to "Nobody" blocks it, and so does declining the call.
NebuSec has not seen the flaw used in real attacks, and believes no one else had realized it could be turned into remote code execution.

articles.title: Linux Kernel TCP Flaw With 9.8 CVSS Score Affects Ubuntu, Red Hat and Other Distributions
articles.summary:
A flaw in the Linux kernel's TCP code, tracked as CVE-2026-98432, affects Ubuntu, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), and other Linux distributions. The kernel's own CVE team rates it 9.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale.
Anthropic said on October 27 that its AI model wrote an exploit that uses the flaw to let a remote attacker with no credentials run commands as root on Linux servers with a multipath TCP listener.
As of October 29, Ubuntu and RHEL have not released a fixed kernel. Red Hat, Amazon, Oracle, and SUSE score the flaw between 5.9 and 8.1, lower than the kernel team's 9.8.
The flaw is a race condition in the code that sets up new IPv4 TCP connections. It can make the kernel read memory it has already freed, a bug type known as a use-after-free.
The kernel fix credits Anthropic researcher Xinyang Ge with reporting the bug. Neither the CVE record nor the fix mentions multipath TCP (MPTCP). The link between that feature and this bug comes from Anthropic's post.
MPTCP lets one connection use several network paths at once. On Linux, an application must request MPTCP when it opens a socket. As of Go 1.24, Go programs do so by default for the sockets they listen on, the Go Security Team said on October 29.
Anthropic's post says the flaw "was patched upstream and backported to all maintained stable kernel branches." For distribution users, that fix arrives only in the vendor's kernel package. Debian, Oracle Linux, SUSE, and Amazon Linux have shipped fixed packages, at least for so…
